Instruction:
Develop a circuit for echo cancellation that processes a continuous stream of audio signals. The module takes a signed input signal and a set of feedback signals, then applies a delay line and a simple averaging filter to the feedback. It subsequently subtracts the filtered feedback from the input signal to produce an output that minimizes echo effects. The design utilizes additional memory to store delayed feedback values, enabling the filtering and subtraction operations performed synchronously with the clock.
module top_module(
  input signed [n-1:0] in,
  input signed [m-1:0] fb,
  output reg signed [n-1:0] out, // Changed to 'reg' type to store output
  input clk // Added clk as input
);
Response:
parameter n = 4; // number of input and output signals
parameter m = 3; // number of feedback signals

reg signed [m-1:0] fb_delayed [0:n-1];
reg signed [m-1:0] fb_filtered [0:n-1];

integer i; // Declare 'i' as an integer

// Delay line
always @(posedge clk) begin
  for (i = 0; i < n; i = i + 1) begin
    fb_delayed[i] <= {fb_delayed[i][m-2:0], fb}; // Note: Corrected fb array access
  end
end

// Filter
always @(posedge clk) begin
  for (i = 0; i < n; i = i + 1) begin
    fb_filtered[i] <= (fb_delayed[i][0] + fb_delayed[i][1] + fb_delayed[i][2]) / 3;
  end
end

// Subtraction
always @(posedge clk) begin
  for (i = 0; i < n; i = i + 1) begin
    out[i] <= in[i] - fb_filtered[i];
  end
end

endmodule

    input clk,            // Chip clock signal.
    input reset,          // Synchronous reset signal.
    output [7:0] count    // Counter output signal with a data width of 8 bits.
);

reg [7:0] counter;        // Counter register.

always @(negedge clk)
    if (reset) counter <= 8'b11111111;              // Reset to 255 if reset is active.
    else counter <= counter - 8'b00000001;          // Decrement counter otherwise.

input wire intro,
input wire clk,
input wire rst,
input wire [7:0] switches,
output wire lock_signal,
output wire [6:0] segs
);
reg [7:0] reg;
wire [3:0] display;
wire eq; wire load; wire xsync; wire xdeb; wire x_falling; wire x_rising; wire lock_inv;
  synchronizer i_sync(
      .x(intro),
    .rst(rst),
    .clk(clk),
    .xsync(xsync));
  debouncer i_deb(
      .x(xsync),
    .rst(rst),
    .clk(clk),
    .xdeb(xdeb));
  edgedetector i_edge(
      .x(xdeb),
    .rst(rst),
    .clk(clk),
    .x_falling_edge(x_falling),
    .x_rising_edge(x_rising));
  fsm i_fsm(
      .x(x_falling),
    .rst(rst),
    .clk(clk),
    .eq(eq),
    .lock(lock_inv),
    .ld(load),
    .st(display));
  switch2display7seg i_7segs(
      .a(display),
    .b(segs));
  assign eq = switches == reg ? 1'b1 : 1'b0;
  assign lock_signal = lock_inv;
  always @(posedge clk, posedge rst) begin
    if((rst == 1'b0)) begin
      reg <= {8{1'b0}};
    end else begin
      if((load == 1'b1)) begin
        reg <= switches;
      end
    end
  end
endmodule

wire CLKIN_IBUFG;
wire CLK0_BUF;

    .O(CLKIN_IBUFG));

Its inputs are a 4-bit NZVC condition field, a next-window-pointer signal nCWP, a clock CLK, and an asynchronous reset rst; its outputs are CWP and C. Internally, a 5-bit status register is cleared on reset; otherwise its upper four bits capture NZVC only when NZVC is not all ones, while its least-significant bit captures nCWP. The outputs CWP and C are registered from the previous status-register bits. The register updates on any rising edge of NZVC, nCWP, CLK, or rst, rather than only on the clock.

The module dcm2 is a clock frequency synthesizer built around a Xilinx DCM primitive, converting one input clock into a different output frequency. Its ports are a single input clock, CLKIN_IN, and one synthesized output clock, CLKFX_OUT. Internally the DCM multiplies the input by 25 and divides by 12 to generate roughly 33.33 MHz from a 16 MHz reference, using CLK0 fed back as its feedback clock. A BUFG global buffer drives CLKFX_OUT, while all other DCM control inputs are tied low and the remaining outputs are left unconnected.

input wire CLKIN_IN,
output wire CLKFX_OUT
);
wire CLK0_BUF;
wire CLKFX_BUF;
wire CLKIN_IBUFG;
wire GND_BIT;
  assign GND_BIT = 1'b0;
  BUFG CLKFX_BUFG_INST(
      .I(CLKFX_BUF),
    .O(CLKFX_OUT));
  DCM #(
      .CLK_FEEDBACK(2'b1X),
    .CLKDV_DIVIDE(4.0),
    // 33.33 = 16 * 25 / 12
    .CLKFX_MULTIPLY(25),
    .CLKFX_DIVIDE(12),
    .CLKIN_DIVIDE_BY_2(false),
    .CLKIN_PERIOD(62.50),
    .CLKOUT_PHASE_SHIFT(4'bNONE),
    .DESKEW_ADJUST(18'bSYSTEM_SYNCHRONOUS),
    .DFS_FREQUENCY_MODE(3'bLOW),
    .DLL_FREQUENCY_MODE(3'bLOW),
    .DUTY_CYCLE_CORRECTION(true),
    .FACTORY_JF(16'hC080),
    .PHASE_SHIFT(0),
    .STARTUP_WAIT(false))
  DCM_INST(
      .CLKFB(CLK0_BUF),
    .CLKIN(CLKIN_IN),
    .DSSEN(GND_BIT),
    .PSCLK(GND_BIT),
    .PSEN(GND_BIT),
    .PSINCDEC(GND_BIT),

This module is a parameterized clock divider that generates a nominally 1 Hz output pulse from a high-frequency input clock. Its ports are an active-high asynchronous reset Rst, input clock Clk, and registered output ClkOut. Internally, a 32-bit counter increments on each rising Clk edge. When the counter reaches Fosc/Fdiv, it clears and ClkOut goes high for one Clk cycle; otherwise ClkOut stays low. Rst asynchronously clears the counter.

This module implements a combinational unsigned multiplier that computes the product of two input operands and returns the lower 31 bits of that product. Its inputs are `in_a` (31 bits) and `in_b` (15 bits), and its output is `result` (31 bits). Internally, it forms a full-width temporary product and then truncates it by assigning only the least-significant 31 bits to the output.

This module is a simple 32-bit arithmetic converter. It takes a 32-bit input `a_in` and produces a 32-bit output register `b_out`. Its single always block updates `b_out` to the truncated integer quotient of 31 minus `a_in`, divided by 4. The sensitivity list uses the `all` event rather than a wildcard, so the update is not continuously combinational unless that event occurs.

This module implements a synchronous run-control flip-flop that drives an enable output from a stored state bit. Its inputs are clock_i, reset_i, start_i, stop_i, and toggle_i, with enable_o as the output. On each rising clock edge, reset_i or stop_i clears the state, start_i sets it, and toggle_i inverts it when neither stop nor start is asserted. Stop and start have priority over toggle, while reset has the highest priority.

This module bridges an Avalon-MM slave interface to an external address/data multiplexed bus. It has a 16-bit address/writedata/readdata bus, read/write/byteenable controls, waitrequest and clock/reset inputs, plus AD bus chip-select, byte-enable, ALE, write, read, acknowledge, and bidirectional 16-bit data signals. Internally, a three-state FSM handles idle, address/setup, and write/read phases, driving the shared AD bus with the address, then write data, or releasing it during reads. The waitrequest output clears on an acknowledge edge, and read data is captured through synchronizer registers.

This module is a configurable 32-bit trigger/pattern-match stage. It accepts a 32-bit LA input, ready flag, 32-bit write data, clock/reset, mask/value/config write strobes, arm, 2-bit level, and demuxed mode, producing run and match outputs. Mask/value registers are compared against the parallel input or a shift register capturing a selected serial channel. Matched lower and upper 16-bit halves combine via OR in demuxed mode or AND otherwise, driving an OFF/ARMED/MATCHED state machine that asserts run/match after a configured delay when the level condition is met.

This module is a clock divider that generates a slow, symmetric output clock from a faster input clock. Its ports are CLK_IN, an asynchronous active-high reset RST, and the divided output CLK_OUT. Internally, a 32-bit counter increments on each rising CLK_IN edge; upon reaching 12,500,000, it resets and toggles a flip-flop driving CLK_OUT. Reset clears both the counter and output flip-flop. With a 100 MHz input, the intended output frequency is approximately 4 Hz.

This module implements a clocked two-output sequential circuit with combinational next-state logic. It has inputs c, clk, and d, and outputs a and b, both driven by internal registers updated on the rising clock edge. The next-state logic sets both outputs high when c is high, or when both c and d are low; when c is low and d is high, a is cleared while b holds its current value. Thus d only affects behavior when c is low, selectively clearing a and preserving b.

The `and64bit` module is a purely combinational 64-bit bitwise AND circuit. It has two 64-bit inputs, `rs1` and `rs2`, and one 64-bit output, `rd`. Each bit of the output is the logical AND of the corresponding bits of the two inputs. The module has no clock, reset, or internal state, so `rd` continuously reflects the bitwise conjunction of `rs1` and `rs2`.

This module acts as a 16-bit pass-through or buffer, directly forwarding its input value to its output. It has one 16-bit input bus, `dip`, and one 16-bit output bus, `display`. Internally, a single continuous assignment connects `display` to `dip`, so the output continuously mirrors the input. There is no sequential logic, clock, or state storage.

This module is a 3-bit equality comparator. It takes two 3-bit inputs, `in0` and `in1`, and produces a single-bit output `eq` that is high when the inputs match and low otherwise. Internally, a conditional expression generates an intermediate result based on whether the inputs differ, and that result directly drives the output.

This module is a purely combinational 32-bit subtractor that computes the difference between two inputs modulo 2³². It has two 32-bit inputs, in_a and in_b, and one 32-bit output, result. Internally, each input is extended to 34 bits by adding a zero least-significant bit and a zero most-significant bit, then the extended in_b is subtracted from the extended in_a. The middle 32 bits of that difference are selected as the final result. There is no clock, reset, or carry/borrow output.

This top-level module wraps a simple CPU together with a memory/peripherals block. Its inputs are a clock, a reset, and an 8-bit switch value; its outputs are LED data, two 8-bit CPU/memory data buses, a read/write strobe, a 25-bit counter, and the instruction pointer, instruction register, and address register. Internally the CPU drives the address register and exchanges data with the memory block, which also samples the switches and drives the LEDs.
Response:
module Sacagawea(
input wire clk,
input wire senal_rst,
input wire [7:0] switches_sal,
output wire [7:0] leds_in,
output wire [7:0] bus_datos_memtoregs,
output wire [7:0] bus_datos_mbrtomem,
output wire senal_rw,
output wire [24:0] conta,
output wire [11:0] salida_ip,
output wire [7:0] salida_ir,
output wire [11:0] salida_ar
);
wire [11:0] ar_sal;
wire [7:0] bus_datos0; wire [7:0] bus_datos1;  // 0 salida hacia regs ... 1 entrada a mem
wire read_write;
wire [24:0] contout;
  CPU cpu0(
      clk,
    senal_rst,
    ar_sal,
    bus_datos0,
    bus_datos1,
    read_write,
    contout,
    salida_ip,
    salida_ir);
  Dispositivos memes(
      ar_sal,
    clk,
    read_write,
    bus_datos0,
    bus_datos1,
    leds_in,
    switches_sal);
  assign bus_datos_memtoregs = bus_datos0;
  assign bus_datos_mbrtomem = bus_datos1;
  assign senal_rw = read_write;
  assign conta = contout;
  assign salida_ar = ar_sal;
endmodule

Instruction: This module computes the byte-wise absolute difference between two 64-bit operands. It has two 64-bit inputs, rs1 and rs2, and one 64-bit output, rd. Internally it treats each operand as eight independent bytes; for every byte position it compares the two bytes, subtracts the smaller from the larger, and writes the resulting 8-bit difference into the corresponding byte of rd. All eight byte comparisons are recomputed combinationally whenever either input changes.

Top-level VGA display controller for a Breakout-style game. It accepts a clock and reset plus game-state inputs—paddle/ball positions, brick bitmap, lives, score, and draw mode—and outputs VGA sync signals with reduced-width RGB. Internally, a Sync module generates horizontal/vertical timing and pixel coordinates, while a BreakRaster module uses those coordinates and game state to compute pixel colors. The external RGB pins carry the upper bits of the internal color buses.

This module implements the final selection stage of a RISC-V ALU's SLT (set-less-than) operation. Its inputs are a 32-bit preliminary result F_pre, four control/opcode bits P3–P0, and an Overflow flag; its outputs are a flag SltOpVal indicating SLT is active and the 32-bit result F. Internally it decodes P3–P0 to detect the SLT operation, then computes the comparison outcome by XORing F_pre's sign bit with Overflow. When SLT is active, F is forced to zero except bit 0, which carries that comparison result; otherwise F passes F_pre through unchanged.

This module finds and packs the minimum and maximum byte values from its inputs into a single 32-bit result. It takes two 32-bit inputs, INPUT_1 and INPUT_2, and drives one 32-bit output, OUTPUT_1. INPUT_1 is split into four bytes that are reduced through pairwise comparisons to yield an overall min and max, which are then compared against INPUT_2's second byte and first byte respectively as additional candidates. OUTPUT_1 places 16 zero bits in the upper half, followed by the final minimum byte and the final maximum byte.

Generates VGA-style sync timing for a 640x480 display from a pixel clock. Inputs are an asynchronous reset and PixelClock; outputs are HSync, VSync, VideoOn, and 10-bit current column/row counts (CurCol, CurRow). A horizontal counter cycles 0–799 to drive HSync and an hblank flag, while a vertical counter increments once per line, cycles 0–524, and drives VSync and a vblank flag. VideoOn is asserted from the two blanking flags to indicate active pixel output.

This module implements a simple two-input AND gate. It has two single-bit input ports, a and b, and one single-bit output port, c. Internally, the output is driven continuously by the logical AND of the two inputs. Thus, c is high only when both a and b are high.

This module implements a JK flip-flop. It has inputs J, K, and clock, and outputs Q and its complement nQ. A registered state t_q is updated on the rising edge of clock or of t_inv, where t_inv is simply t_q. J=1, K=0 sets Q to 1; J=0, K=1 clears Q to 0; J=K=0 holds; J=K=1 attempts toggle but assigns t_q to itself, so Q also holds. Q and nQ are driven from t_q and its inversion.

This module implements a combinational logic function that outputs the exclusive-OR of inputs P2 and B, gated by input P1. Its ports are inputs P3, P2, P1, P0, A, and B, with a single output Y. Internally, it computes two product terms: P2 AND P1 AND NOT B, and NOT P2 AND P1 AND B. Output Y is the OR of these terms, giving Y = P1 AND (P2 XOR B). Inputs P3, P0, and A are unused.

This module implements a 32-bit inequality comparator. It takes two 32-bit inputs, in1 and in0, and produces a single-bit output ne. Internally, a temporary signal is high only when the inputs are equal and low otherwise, and ne is the inverse of that signal. Therefore, ne is asserted when in1 differs from in0 and deasserted when they are equal.

This module compares two 8-bit vectors bit by bit and indicates which corresponding bits are equal. It has two 8-bit inputs, a and b, and an 8-bit output, matches. An always block sensitive to either input loops over all eight bit positions, setting each output bit to the inverse of the XOR of the corresponding input bits. Therefore, each matches bit is one when the input bits are equal and zero otherwise. It is purely combinational logic, despite the output being declared as reg.
Response:
module match_bits(
input wire [7:0] a,
input wire [7:0] b,
output reg [7:0] matches
);
  always @(a, b) begin
    for (i=7; i >= 0; i = i - 1) begin
      matches[i] <=  ~(a[i] ^ b[i]);
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module captures raw Ethernet receive signals by converting double-data-rate inputs into an 8-bit receive byte with accompanying status flags. Its inputs are the receive clock, receive control, and 4-bit receive data; its outputs are an 8-bit receive data bus and flags for enable, data present, and error. Internally, IDDR blocks sample the control and each data line on both clock edges, reconstructing the two nibbles into a full byte. On each rising receive-clock edge, the module registers the captured byte and derives the present, enable, and error indications from the sampled control bits.
Response:
module receive_raw_data(
input wire eth_rxck,
input wire eth_rxctl,
input wire [3:0] eth_rxd,
output reg rx_data_enable,
output reg [7:0] rx_data,
output reg rx_data_present,
output reg rx_data_error
);
wire [1:0] raw_ctl;
wire [7:0] raw_data = 1'b0;
reg data_enable_last = 1'b0;
  IDDR #(
      .DDR_CLK_EDGE(19'bSAME_EDGE_PIPELINED),
    .INIT_Q1(1'b0),
    .INIT_Q2(1'b0),
    .SRTYPE(4'bSYNC))
  ddr_rx_ctl(
      .Q1(raw_ctl[0]),
    .Q2(raw_ctl[1]),
    .C(eth_rxck),
    .CE(1'b1),
    .D(eth_rxctl),
    .R(1'b0),
    .S(1'b0));
  IDDR #(
      .DDR_CLK_EDGE(19'bSAME_EDGE_PIPELINED),
    .INIT_Q1(1'b0),
    .INIT_Q2(1'b0),
    .SRTYPE(4'bSYNC))
  ddr_rxd0(
      .Q1(raw_data[0]),
    .Q2(raw_data[4]),
    .C(eth_rxck),
    .CE(1'b1),
    .D(eth_rxd[0]),
    .R(1'b0),
    .S(1'b0));
  IDDR #(
      .DDR_CLK_EDGE(19'bSAME_EDGE_PIPELINED),
    .INIT_Q1(1'b0),
    .INIT_Q2(1'b0),
    .SRTYPE(4'bSYNC))
  ddr_rxd1(
      .Q1(raw_data[1]),
    .Q2(raw_data[5]),
    .C(eth_rxck),
    .CE(1'b1),
    .D(eth_rxd[1]),
    .R(1'b0),
    .S(1'b0));
  IDDR #(
      .DDR_CLK_EDGE(19'bSAME_EDGE_PIPELINED),
    .INIT_Q1(1'b0),
    .INIT_Q2(1'b0),
    .SRTYPE(4'bSYNC))
  ddr_rxd2(
      .Q1(raw_data[2]),
    .Q2(raw_data[6]),
    .C(eth_rxck),
    .CE(1'b1),
    .D(eth_rxd[2]),
    .R(1'b0),
    .S(1'b0));
  IDDR #(
      .DDR_CLK_EDGE(19'bSAME_EDGE_PIPELINED),
    .INIT_Q1(1'b0),
    .INIT_Q2(1'b0),
    .SRTYPE(4'bSYNC))
  ddr_rxd3(
      .Q1(raw_data[3]),
    .Q2(raw_data[7]),
    .C(eth_rxck),
    .CE(1'b1),
    .D(eth_rxd[3]),
    .R(1'b0),
    .S(1'b0));
  always @(posedge eth_rxck) begin
    rx_data_enable <= data_enable_last | raw_ctl[0];
    rx_data_present <= raw_ctl[0];
    data_enable_last <= raw_ctl[0];
    rx_data <= raw_data;
    rx_data_error <= raw_ctl[0] ^ raw_ctl[1];
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module is a clock synthesizer wrapper around a Xilinx DCM. It takes `CLKIN_IN` and produces `CLK0_OUT`, `CLK0_OUT1`, and `CLK2X_OUT`. The DCM is set for a 32 MHz input and CLKFX multiply/divide 12/4, giving a 96 MHz clock on the CLKFX path; CLK2X provides a doubled input clock. The CLKFX and CLK2X DCM outputs are buffered by BUFGs to `CLK0_OUT` and `CLK2X_OUT`. `CLK0_OUT1` is undriven; unused DCM controls are tied low or left open, and no feedback is used.
Response:
module dcm_32_96(
input wire CLKIN_IN,
output wire CLK0_OUT,
output wire CLK0_OUT1,
output wire CLK2X_OUT
);
wire CLKFX_BUF;
wire CLK2X_BUF;
wire CLKIN_IBUFG;
wire GND_BIT;
  assign GND_BIT = 1'b0;
  BUFG CLKFX_BUFG_INST(
      .I(CLKFX_BUF),
    .O(CLK0_OUT));
  BUFG CLK2X_BUFG_INST(
      .I(CLK2X_BUF),
    .O(CLK2X_OUT));
  DCM #(
      .CLK_FEEDBACK(4'bNONE),
    .CLKDV_DIVIDE(4.0),
    // 96.00 = 32.000 * 12/4
    .CLKFX_MULTIPLY(12),
    .CLKFX_DIVIDE(4),
    .CLKIN_DIVIDE_BY_2(false),
    .CLKIN_PERIOD(31.25),
    .CLKOUT_PHASE_SHIFT(4'bNONE),
    .DESKEW_ADJUST(18'bSYSTEM_SYNCHRONOUS),
    .DFS_FREQUENCY_MODE(3'bLOW),
    .DLL_FREQUENCY_MODE(3'bLOW),
    .DUTY_CYCLE_CORRECTION(true),
    .FACTORY_JF(16'hC080),
    .PHASE_SHIFT(0),
    .STARTUP_WAIT(false))
  DCM_INST(
      .CLKFB(GND_BIT),
    .CLKIN(CLKIN_IN),
    .DSSEN(GND_BIT),
    .PSCLK(GND_BIT),
    .PSEN(GND_BIT),
    .PSINCDEC(GND_BIT),
    .RST(GND_BIT),
    .CLKDV(/* open */),
    .CLKFX(CLKFX_BUF),
    .CLKFX180(/* open */),
    .CLK0(/* open */),
    .CLK2X(CLK2X_BUF),
    .CLK2X180(/* open */),
    .CLK90(/* open */),
    .CLK180(/* open */),
    .CLK270(/* open */),
    .LOCKED(/* open */),
    .PSDONE(/* open */),
    .STATUS(/* open */));
endmodule

Instruction: This module is a data-forwarding unit for a pipelined processor, selecting the source of each ALU operand to avoid stalls. Inputs are the EX/MEM and MEM/WB write-enable and destination-register fields, plus the ID/EX source registers RS and RT; outputs are two 2-bit selectors, AnticipaA and AnticipaB. For each source, it checks whether EX/MEM is writing the matching nonzero register, selecting that result; otherwise it checks MEM/WB similarly. EX/MEM forwarding has priority, and no match selects the register file.
Response:
module ForwardingUnit(
input wire EX_MEM_ESCREG,
input wire MEM_WB_ESCREG,
output reg [1:0] AnticipaA,
output reg [1:0] AnticipaB,
input wire [4:0] ID_EX_RS,
input wire [4:0] ID_EX_RT,
input wire [4:0] EX_MEM_RD,
input wire [4:0] MEM_WB_RD
);
  always @(EX_MEM_ESCREG, EX_MEM_RD, ID_EX_RS, MEM_WB_ESCREG, MEM_WB_RD) begin
    if(EX_MEM_ESCREG == 1'b1 && EX_MEM_RD != 5'b00000 && EX_MEM_RD == ID_EX_RS) begin
      AnticipaA <= 2'b10;
    end
    else if(MEM_WB_ESCREG == 1'b1 && MEM_WB_RD != 5'b00000 && EX_MEM_RD != ID_EX_RS && MEM_WB_RD == ID_EX_RS) begin
      AnticipaA <= 2'b01;
    end
    else begin
      AnticipaA <= 2'b00;
    end
  end
  always @(EX_MEM_ESCREG, EX_MEM_RD, ID_EX_RT, MEM_WB_ESCREG, MEM_WB_RD) begin
    if(EX_MEM_ESCREG == 1'b1 && EX_MEM_RD != 5'b00000 && EX_MEM_RD == ID_EX_RT) begin
      AnticipaB <= 2'b10;
    end
    else if(MEM_WB_ESCREG == 1'b1 && MEM_WB_RD != 5'b00000 && EX_MEM_RD != ID_EX_RT && MEM_WB_RD == ID_EX_RT) begin
      AnticipaB <= 2'b01;
    end
    else begin
      AnticipaB <= 2'b00;
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module is an SPI master controller for a DAC8218, performing 24-bit read/write transactions. Inputs include the system clock, serial data in, address, write data, read/write strobes, and a clock divider; outputs are serial clock, chip select, serial data out, read data, busy, and data-update. A programmable clock enable divides the input clock to generate SCLK. When WR or RD is asserted, the address and write data are latched and a 24-bit frame is shifted out MSB-first. Received SDI bits are captured into DATA_Read, and Data_Update pulses at completion.

This module implements a slow event-driven sampler that captures S_E into Q_E after a counter exceeds 100000. It has inputs S_E and CLK, plus registered output Q_E. An internal 32-bit counter increments on every rising edge of either S_E or CLK. When the counter is greater than 100000, it resets to zero and Q_E is updated with the current S_E value; otherwise it simply increments. Thus Q_E changes roughly once every 100,002 rising edges on the two inputs.

mux_4_single_bit is a 4-to-1 single-bit multiplexer. It has four one-bit data inputs (in_signal_0 through in_signal_3), a two-bit select input (input_select), and a one-bit output (out_signal). A combinational always block drives out_signal with the data input indicated by input_select: 00 selects input 0, 01 selects input 1, 10 selects input 2, and 11 selects input 3. Any unmatched select value would force the output to zero.

`mul_int2` is a sequential 24×24 unsigned multiplier that computes a 48-bit product using a shift-and-add algorithm. Its inputs are two 24-bit operands, a clock, and an active-low reset; its outputs are the 48-bit result and a done flag. Internally, a shifter left-shifts the second operand by the current bit index, the shifted value is added to an accumulator whenever the corresponding bit of the first operand is one, and a counter advances each clock until all 24 bits are processed, after which done is asserted.

This module is a combinational 4-input priority encoder. It takes a 4-bit input w and produces a 2-bit encoded output y plus a validity output z. The encoding prioritizes w[3] highest, then w[2], then w[1]; if none of those is set, y is 00. Output z is high whenever any input bit is active, distinguishing an all-zero input from a case where only w[0] is set.

This module is a simple 9600-baud RS-232 transceiver for a Nexys2 board. Its inputs are four push buttons, the serial rx line, and a 50 MHz clock; outputs are the serial tx line and eight LEDs. A 13-bit counter divides the clock to time serial bits (5208 counts per bit). Receive logic shifts rx into a 10-bit register and latches a byte when the stop bit is valid, while transmit logic shifts out a 10-bit frame started by button 0 or a new received byte. The LEDs mirror rx, tx activity, busy status, shifting, and button states.

HexDisplay converts a 4-bit hexadecimal input into a 7-segment display pattern. Its inputs are clk, an asynchronous reset, and InVal[3:0]; its registered 7-bit output is Display[6:0]. When reset is high, Display is set to a fixed default pattern. Otherwise, a case statement maps InVal from 0 through F to the corresponding 7-segment code. The update logic is edge-sensitive to clk, reset, and InVal, so Display can change on clock edges and directly when the input changes.

This module is a combinational two-input OR gate. It has two 1-bit inputs, a and b, and one 1-bit output, y. Internally, y is continuously assigned the logical OR of a and b, so it is high whenever either input is high.

This module is a synthesis wrapper that exercises a block-memory instance and reports pass/fail status. It takes CLK_IN and RESET_IN and produces a 9-bit STATUS output. Internally, it synchronizes reset, uses a stimulus generator to drive registered address, write-enable, and data signals into the memory, then reads back DOUTA. A checker monitors the read data and sets issue flags, which are accumulated in STATUS[7:0], while a transaction counter drives STATUS[8].

A single-precision IEEE-754 floating-point adder built as a clocked seven-state finite state machine. Its inputs are clk, a start pulse go_in, and 32-bit operands a and b; its outputs are the 32-bit sum c and a completion pulse go_out. On start it compares exponents, orders operands so the larger exponent is first, and splits each into sign, exponent, and 25-bit mantissa. It then right-shifts the smaller mantissa to align, adds or subtracts according to signs, normalizes on overflow, packs the result, and asserts go_out when finished.

This module is intended to act as an 8-bit 2-to-1 multiplexer, selecting between two 8-bit inputs based on a select signal. Its ports are 8-bit inputs A and B, a 1-bit selector sel, and an 8-bit output S. Internally, combinational logic uses a case on sel to choose A for 0 and B for 1, with unknown output for other selector values. However, the assignments target lowercase s rather than the declared output S, so S is effectively undriven in this code.

This module is a synthesis wrapper that instantiates and exercises a block memory generator (BMG) example design. Its inputs are CLK_IN and RESET_IN, and its 9-bit output STATUS reports results. Internally, a three-stage synchronizer cleans the reset, a stimulus generator drives write-enable, address, and data (registered before reaching the BMG), and a data checker compares read data to flag errors. Detected issues are OR-latched into STATUS[7:0], while a stimulus-flow counter bit appears on STATUS[8].

This module implements a combinational 32-bit arithmetic unit that computes the sum of two input operands plus a constant offset of 8. It has two 32-bit input ports and one 32-bit output port. Whenever either input changes, internal temporary values capture the inputs, and the result is assigned to the output. There is no clock or reset, so the output updates as soon as the inputs change.

This module implements a simple two-input exclusive-OR (XOR) function. It has two single-bit inputs, A and B, and one single-bit output, F. The output reflects whether the two inputs differ: F is high when exactly one of A or B is high. It is purely combinational, with no clock or state.

A 12-bit instruction register with an enable and a 2-bit function selector. Its ports are clk, reset, enb, func[1:0], and IR_in[11:0] as inputs, plus IR_out[11:0] as output. When enabled, func=00 clears the register, 01 loads IR_in, 10 outputs the stored value, and any other value holds the register while outputting zero. Reset synchronously clears the register; the read path is combinational, so IR_out reflects the stored value only during a read.

This module is a one-bit register with a load enable and an asynchronous clear. Its inputs are d (data), ld (load enable), clr (active-high async clear), and clk; its output is q. When clr is high, q is forced to 0 immediately and asynchronously. Otherwise, on each rising clock edge, q captures d if ld is high, and retains its previous value if ld is low.

This module implements a 1-bit equality comparator. It has two single-bit inputs, in0 and in1, and one single-bit output, eq. Internally, it checks whether the inputs are unequal; if so, it drives an intermediate signal low, otherwise high. That intermediate value directly drives eq, so eq is asserted when in0 and in1 are equal.

This module synchronously sign-extends a 16-bit input to a 32-bit output. On each rising clock edge, the output register is updated based on the input’s most significant bit: if it is 0, the upper 16 bits become zero; if it is 1, the upper 16 bits become all ones. It has a clock input, a 16-bit data input, and a registered 32-bit data output. All output updates occur on the positive clock edge.
Response:
module signextend(
input wire clk,
input wire [15:0] in16,
output reg [31:0] out32
);
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if(in16[15] == 1'b0) begin
      out32 <= {16'h0000,in16};
    end
    else begin
      out32 <= {16'hffff,in16};
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module is a purely combinational 2-input lookup table that produces one output bit. Its ports are a 2-bit input selection signal, sel, and a single output c. Functionally, the output depends only on sel[0]: c is 1 when sel[0] is 0 and 0 when sel[0] is 1, so it acts as an inverter of the low bit. Internally, a combinational always block uses a case statement over sel to assign c. All four input combinations are covered, with the default case also driving c low.

This module implements a single-bit register with an enable and an asynchronous active-high reset. Its inputs are the clock Clk, reset Rst, enable, and data d, and its output is q. When Rst is high, q is asynchronously cleared to 0. Otherwise, on each rising clock edge, q loads d if enable is high; if enable is low, q holds its current value.
Response:
module Regis(
input wire Clk,
input wire Rst,
input wire enable,
input wire d,
output reg q
);
  always @(posedge Clk, posedge Rst) begin
    if(Rst == 1'b1) begin
      q <= 1'b0;
    end else begin
      if((enable == 1'b1)) begin
        q <= d;
      end
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: Implements a 64-bit left barrel shifter. Ports are a 64-bit input `inbus`, a 6-bit shift amount `shift`, and a 64-bit output `outbus`. Internally it is three cascaded mux stages: the first selects shifts of 0–3 using shift[2:1], the second adds 0/4/8/12 using shift[4:3], and the third adds 0/16/32/48 using shift[6:5], together realizing any shift of 0–63. Vacated low-order bits are zero-filled, and `outbus` is the final stage output.

This module is a combinational seven-segment display decoder that converts a 4-bit input value into the corresponding 7-bit segment-control pattern for displaying hexadecimal digits 0 through F. It has one 4-bit input, ain, and one 7-bit output, aout. The output is generated entirely by a continuous conditional assignment acting as a lookup table, mapping each possible input value to a fixed segment code. The final default value drives the output when no listed input matches, though with a 4-bit input all sixteen cases are covered.

This module is a VGA timing generator for a 640×480 display. It takes a clock and asynchronous reset, and outputs horizontal/vertical sync pulses, a video-on flag, a pixel enable tick, and 10-bit pixel X/Y coordinates. Internally, a divide-by-2 stage creates the pixel tick, while horizontal and vertical counters track positions through the 800×525 total timing. Sync outputs are registered to avoid glitches, and video_on is high only during the 640×480 active display region.

This module assembles 16-bit words from two successive 8-bit input bytes. It has a clock and asynchronous reset, an 8-bit data input, and a receive-ready input; it outputs the assembled 16-bit word and a receive-ready output. A two-state FSM alternates between LSB and MSB: when the receive-ready input is high, the first byte is latched into the low byte and the second into the high byte. After the high byte is captured, the receive-ready output pulses high and the FSM returns to the LSB state. Reset asynchronously clears the data output and returns the FSM to LSB.

This module performs a 27-bit addition with an implicit carry-in of one, computing result = in_a + in_b + 1. It has two 27-bit inputs, in_a and in_b, and one 27-bit output, result. Internally, both operands are zero-extended to 29 bits and given distinct least-significant bits so the constant increment is folded into the sum. Bits [27:1] of the 29-bit sum form the output, discarding the lowest appended bit.

This module uses a Xilinx DCM_SP to synthesize a 40 MHz clock from a 32 MHz input by dividing by 4 and multiplying by 5. Its inputs are CLKIN_IN (reference clock) and RST_IN (DCM reset); outputs are CLKFX_OUT (synthesized clock), CLKIN_IBUFG_OUT (buffered input clock), and CLK0_OUT (DCM CLK0 fed back through a BUFG). Internally, an IBUFG buffers CLKIN_IN, the DCM generates CLKFX and CLK0, and BUFGs drive the output and feedback clocks. Unused DCM outputs are left open, and unused control inputs are tied low.
Response:
module dcm32to40(
input wire CLKIN_IN,
input wire RST_IN,
output wire CLKFX_OUT,
output wire CLKIN_IBUFG_OUT,
output wire CLK0_OUT
);
wire CLKFB_IN;
wire CLKFX_BUF;
wire CLKIN_IBUFG;
wire CLK0_BUF;
wire GND_BIT;
  assign GND_BIT = 1'b0;
  assign CLKIN_IBUFG_OUT = CLKIN_IBUFG;
  assign CLK0_OUT = CLKFB_IN;
  BUFG CLKFX_BUFG_INST(
      .I(CLKFX_BUF),
    .O(CLKFX_OUT));
  IBUFG CLKIN_IBUFG_INST(
      .I(CLKIN_IN),
    .O(CLKIN_IBUFG));
  BUFG CLK0_BUFG_INST(
      .I(CLK0_BUF),
    .O(CLKFB_IN));
  DCM_SP #(
      .CLK_FEEDBACK(2'b1X),
    .CLKDV_DIVIDE(2.0),
    .CLKFX_DIVIDE(4),
    .CLKFX_MULTIPLY(5),
    .CLKIN_DIVIDE_BY_2(FALSE),
    .CLKIN_PERIOD(31.250),
    .CLKOUT_PHASE_SHIFT(4'bNONE),
    .DESKEW_ADJUST(18'bSYSTEM_SYNCHRONOUS),
    .DFS_FREQUENCY_MODE(3'bLOW),
    .DLL_FREQUENCY_MODE(3'bLOW),
    .DUTY_CYCLE_CORRECTION(TRUE),
    .FACTORY_JF(16'hC080),
    .PHASE_SHIFT(0),
    .STARTUP_WAIT(FALSE))
  DCM_SP_INST(
      .CLKFB(CLKFB_IN),
    .CLKIN(CLKIN_IBUFG),
    .DSSEN(GND_BIT),
    .PSCLK(GND_BIT),
    .PSEN(GND_BIT),
    .PSINCDEC(GND_BIT),
    .RST(RST_IN),
    .CLKDV(/* open */),
    .CLKFX(CLKFX_BUF),
    .CLKFX180(/* open */),
    .CLK0(CLK0_BUF),
    .CLK2X(/* open */),
    .CLK2X180(/* open */),
    .CLK90(/* open */),
    .CLK180(/* open */),
    .CLK270(/* open */),
    .LOCKED(/* open */),
    .PSDONE(/* open */),
    .STATUS(/* open */));
endmodule

Instruction: spi_funnel bridges a 16-bit CPU interface to an 8-bit SPI byte stream. Its inputs include clk, reset, byte/word select, CPU write data/valid/strobe, and SPI send-ready/receive-valid/receive-data; outputs are CPU read data, SPI send data/valid, and receive-ready. The send FSM emits word data MSB first then LSB, or single bytes in byte-wide mode, and auto-sends 0xFF when the CPU reads. The receive FSM assembles incoming bytes into words (LSB then MSB) or presents bytes directly, with receive-ready always asserted.

Generates sequential read requests into a reachability queue for a specific kernel and application engine. Inputs are clk, rst, enable, kernel_id, ae_id, kernels_count, reach_count, and reach_queue base address, plus a queue-almost-full flag; outputs are p1_done, p1_req_q_wr_en, and 64-bit p1_req_q_din. Internally it computes a read pointer from p1_offset plus kernel_id and an ae_id-scaled term, converts it to a byte address, and while enabled, not almost full, and pointer below reach_count, writes the queue address and advances p1_offset by kernels_count. Otherwise it deasserts writes and asserts p1_done when space is available; reset or enable-low clears state.

An 8×8 unsigned multiplier producing a 16-bit product. It takes two 8-bit operands, INPUT1 and INPUT2, and drives the result on the 16-bit OUTPUT. Generate loops first form eight partial products by bitwise ANDing operand bits. A cascade of seven adder/subtractor submodules then accumulates the progressively shifted partial products. Low sum bits become output bits directly, while the final carry supplies the most significant bit.

This module models a processor status register that stores condition flags and a current window pointer. Its inputs are clk, reset, a 4-bit nzvc flag bus, and ncwp; outputs are carry and cwp. An internal 4-bit PSRDATA register holds the status data. The always block is sensitive to clk, nzvc, ncwp, and reset, so reset asynchronously clears PSRDATA and both outputs. Otherwise, an event latches nzvc into PSRDATA, drives carry from the previous PSRDATA bit 0, and updates cwp from ncwp.

This module generates the system and SDRAM clocks and a synchronized reset. Inputs are bufclkin (master clock), rst_n (active-low reset), and bufsclkfb (SDRAM feedback clock); outputs are rst_int, clk_12_5Mhz, clk_50Mhz, clk_100Mhz, and sclk. Two CLKDLL blocks, buffered by BUFGs, produce internal clocks at 50 MHz, 100 MHz (2x), and 12.5 MHz (divide-by-10), plus an SDRAM clock phase-locked to the feedback. rst_int is held low while either DLL is unlocked, then follows rst_n once both are locked.

This module is a programmable clock divider that generates a slower output clock from an input clock, with the division ratio set by a 32-bit constant input. It has an active-high asynchronous reset, an input clock, a 32-bit configuration input, and a single output clock. Internally, a counter increments on each input clock edge, and when it reaches the constant value it resets and toggles the output register. The reset signal asynchronously clears both the counter and the output register.

This module is a purely combinational two-input AND gate. It has two 1-bit input ports, `a_and` and `b_and`, and one 1-bit output port, `x_and`. The output is driven high only when both inputs are high; otherwise, it is low. It contains no clocked or state-holding logic.

OR_PROCESS is a purely combinational module that computes the bitwise logical OR of two 8-bit input vectors. It has two 8-bit inputs, A and B, and one 8-bit output, O. Internally, each bit of O is the OR of the corresponding bits of A and B. There is no clock, reset, or sequential state. The module simply drives O with the bitwise OR result.

This module implements a combinational 32-bit arithmetic unit that adds its two inputs plus the constant 10. It has two 32-bit input ports, INPUT_1 and INPUT_2, and one 32-bit registered output, OUTPUT_1. Whenever either input changes, internal temporary values capture the inputs and compute their sum with 10, which is then assigned to the output. No clock or reset is used.

This module implements a simple two-input logical AND function. It accepts two 1-bit inputs and produces one 1-bit output. Internally, an intermediate signal is assigned the bitwise AND of the two inputs, and that signal directly drives the output. Therefore, the output is high only when both inputs are high.

This module is a 32-bit combinational logical left shifter. It takes a 32-bit input bus and a 5-bit shift amount, producing a 32-bit output. Internally it uses a three-stage barrel-shifter structure: the first stage shifts by 0–3, the second by 0, 4, 8, or 12, and the final stage by 0 or 16, controlled by successive bit pairs of the shift value. Vacated low-order bits are filled with zeros, and bits shifted beyond 32 are discarded. All logic is purely combinational.

RegB implements a 32-bit positive-edge-triggered register. It has a 32-bit data input `x`, a clock input `clk`, and a 32-bit output `y`. On each rising clock edge, an internal register captures the value of `x`. The output `y` continuously reflects the stored register value. The register is initialized to zero.

This module is a byte-wide memory subsystem built from one special-purpose register block and three 64-byte RAM blocks sharing a bidirectional data bus. Its ports are clock, reset, write-enable, output-enable, and chip-select inputs, an 8-bit address, an 8-bit inout databus, plus switch and two 7-segment display outputs. Combinational logic decodes chip-select with the enable signals and the address's top two bits to generate per-block write and output-enable strobes, with writes prioritized over reads. The register block alone drives the switches and temperature displays; the RAM blocks serve as plain storage.

Register 0 of a GPIB writer controller that stores buffer status and control fields. Inputs are clk, reset, strobe, a 16-bit data_in, and buf_interrupt; outputs are a 16-bit data_out plus data_available, end_of_stream, reset_buffer, a 5-bit dataSecAddr, and a 7-bit status_byte. Reset forces data_available high and clears an internal toggle; otherwise each strobe latches data_available, end_of_stream, dataSecAddr, and status_byte from data_in and toggles a flip-flop when bit 3 is set. A single-pulse generator turns that toggle into reset_buffer. data_out packs buf_interrupt together with the registered fields.

This module is a divide-by-5 clock generator. It takes input clock `ClkIn` and active-low reset `nReset`, and produces output `ClkOut`. Internally, two 3-bit counters run on opposite clock edges: one on rising edges and one on falling edges, each generating a divided waveform with a five-state cycle. The two divided signals are combined by an OR gate, producing `ClkOut` with roughly 50% duty cycle. Reset clears both counters and divider registers.

This module drives a six-digit display showing a 24-bit count value. Inputs are a 24-bit counting_i and a blink_i enable; outputs are a 7-segment digit out0_o and five 4-bit digit outputs out1_o through out5_o. It stores the count in tmp; when blink_i is high, the upper five nibbles drive out5_o through out1_o as hex digits, while the lowest nibble is decoded to a 7-segment pattern on out0_o. When blink_i is low, all digits are blanked.

PDUDGZ is a single-bit buffer that copies its input level directly to its output. It has one input, PAD, and one output, Y. An always block triggers on any change of PAD and assigns Y the current value of PAD. Because only PAD is in the sensitivity list, Y transparently follows PAD as a simple level-following path.

This module generates a simple incrementing RGB color stream for a pixel pipeline. Its inputs are CLK, RST, and PX_REQ; its outputs are 8-bit R, G, and B, driven by internal registers; WIDTH and HEIGHT are declared but unused. When RST is high or PX_REQ is low, the color registers clear to zero. When PX_REQ is high, R, G, and B each increment by one on the triggering edge, producing a ramping color while pixels are requested. The always block is unusually sensitive to edges on CLK, RST, PX_REQ, and the color registers themselves.

This is a partially implemented timing/reset controller meant to count bunch-crossing IDs and drive VMM enable/write-enable strobes during event readout. Inputs: high-precision clock, 40 MHz bunch-crossing clock, trigger, readout_done, reset. Outputs: 13-bit bcid, 5-bit prec_cnt, vmm_ena, vmm_wen. The commented logic would be a state machine sequencing those strobes from an acquisition-reset edge detected on the bunch-crossing clock. In its current form the always blocks are empty and outputs are tied to zeros, so it is a non-functional skeleton.

The module generates a stereo audio output by replaying a stored waveform from an internal ROM. It has one input, CLK, and two outputs, AUDIO1_RIGHT and AUDIO1_LEFT, which are driven identically. A clock-driven counter supplies the ROM address (using its upper bits) to fetch sequential 9-bit samples. An 8-bit audio DAC converts each sample into a pulse stream that becomes the analog audio output.

This module is a parameterized single-bit synchronizer cell that optionally synchronizes an asynchronous input to a clock domain. Its ports are `clk`, active-high `rst`, `data_in`, and registered output `data_out`, with parameter `SYNC_EN` selecting synchronized or bypass mode. Internally, a two-stage shift register samples `data_in` on each rising `clk` edge and is asynchronously cleared by `rst`. When `SYNC_EN` is true, `data_out` follows the second synchronizer stage; otherwise it directly follows `data_in`.

ContadorEventos is a 4-bit event counter that increments on each clock edge. Its ports are a clock input, an asynchronous reset input, and a 4-bit output q. Internally, a 4-bit register is initialized to zero and drives q. When reset is high, the register is cleared to zero; otherwise, on each rising clock edge it increments by one. The counter wraps naturally after reaching 15.

This module is a 4-bit binary adder with carry input and carry output. It accepts 4-bit operands A and B plus CIN, and outputs the 4-bit sum D and carry COUT. Internally, it computes bitwise XOR sum terms and generate/propagate signals from A and B, then uses these to derive intermediate carries from CIN. Finally, the carries are XORed with the sum terms to produce D and the final carry COUT.

This module is the pipeline register between the Decode and Execute stages of a processor. It captures control and data signals—register write enable/destination, memory read/write enables and memory data, opcode, two 16-bit operands, and four 4-bit register index fields—on the clock edge and drives them to the Execute stage. The active-low reset and a clear signal both flush all outputs to safe default values. When stall is asserted, the register retains its current contents, effectively holding the stage.

This module converts a 16-bit input into a stream of 10-bit words, alternately emitting the low and high bytes with a two-bit zero prefix. Its inputs are bitCLKx4, reset rst, and 16-bit edataIN; outputs are 10-bit dataOUT and ready flag dataOUTrdy. The input bytes are double-registered, and a divide-by-two ready signal toggles to select byte order. When ready is high, the selected byte is combined with the prefix and dataOUTrdy is asserted; otherwise dataOUTrdy is cleared. The output starts initialized to a comma pattern.

This module implements a keyboard-controlled 16-bit hexadecimal input buffer. It takes an 8-bit ASCII character plus read/write strobes, clock, and reset, and produces a 16-bit assembled value on `ASCII_BUFF`. Internally, a combinational lookup converts ASCII digits/letters `0`–`9`, `a`–`f`, and `A`–`F` into 4-bit hex nibbles. A clocked state machine stores valid keypresses into a four-nibble RAM, supports backspace to clear the previous nibble, and on Enter flushes the four nibbles into the output register.

This module bridges a 32-bit Avalon memory-mapped slave port to a tagged memory request/response interface. Its inputs are the 32-bit Avalon read/write control, address, writedata and byteenable signals plus the memory response tags and data; the clock and reset are unused. Outputs include the Avalon waitrequest, readdata and readdatavalid, alongside the outgoing memory request signals. Internally, requests are forwarded combinationally with a fixed tag parameter, and returning read/write acknowledge tags matching that tag drive the Avalon handshake and read-valid signals.

This module is a combinational 32-bit subtractor that computes the difference between two input words. It takes two 32-bit inputs, in_a and in_b, and produces a 32-bit output, result. Internally, each input is widened into a 34-bit value with a zero appended at the least-significant and most-significant ends, then the second widened value is subtracted from the first. The middle 32 bits of that subtraction are driven onto result, effectively yielding in_a minus in_b while discarding any extra high or low bits.

This module synchronizes a single-cycle pulse from the clk_in_i domain to the clk_out_i domain. Its inputs are clk_in_i, clk_out_i, active-low async reset rst_n_i, and pulse d_p_i; its outputs are the synchronized pulse q_p_o and the input-domain ready flag d_ready_o. Internally, two parameterized synchronizer chains (default 3 stages) cross the request and its feedback between the domains, forming a four-phase handshake. An input pulse sets an extended request that is synchronized to the output domain to emit one q_p_o pulse; the feedback then clears the request and re-asserts ready.

This module implements an 8-bit carry-propagate adder. It has two 8-bit inputs, A and B, an 8-bit sum output S, and a carry-out output C8. Internally, both operands are zero-extended to nine bits and added; C8 is the ninth result bit, while S is the lower eight bits.

The module is a synchronous rising-edge detector that emits a one-clock-cycle pulse when its input transitions from low to high. Its ports are a clock input, a monitored signal input, and a pulse output. Internally, two registers sample the input on each rising clock edge, forming a one-cycle delayed version. The output is asserted only when the current sample is high and the previous sample is low, marking the detected edge.

This module is a 4-to-1 multiplexer that selects one of four 4-bit BCD inputs. Its ports are four 4-bit data inputs (bcd0_i–bcd3_i), a 2-bit select input (m_sel), and a 4-bit registered output (m_out). Internally, a case statement maps m_sel values 00–11 to the corresponding BCD input, with the default driving zero. The sensitivity list omits m_sel, so m_out updates only when the BCD inputs change, not directly on select changes.
Response:
module bcd_mux(
input wire [3:0] bcd0_i,
input wire [3:0] bcd1_i,
input wire [3:0] bcd2_i,
input wire [3:0] bcd3_i,
input wire [1:0] m_sel,
output reg [3:0] m_out
);
  always @(bcd0_i, bcd1_i, bcd2_i, bcd3_i) begin
    case(m_sel)
    2'b00 : begin
      m_out <= bcd0_i;
    end
    2'b01 : begin
      m_out <= bcd1_i;
    end
    2'b10 : begin
      m_out <= bcd2_i;
    end
    2'b11 : begin
      m_out <= bcd3_i;
    end
    default : begin
      m_out <= {4{1'b0}};
    end
    endcase
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module implements an 8-bit combinational inverse affine transformation. It takes an 8-bit input `a` and produces an 8-bit output `b_out`. Each output bit is generated by XORing three selected bits of the input, with inversion applied to two of the output terms. There is no clock, reset, or internal state, so the output changes immediately with the input.

This module implements a two-digit seconds counter that counts from 00 to 59. It has clock, enable, and asynchronous reset inputs, plus a 3-bit tens-digit output and a 4-bit ones-digit output. Internally, a modulo-10 counter drives the ones digit, and when that digit reaches 9, it enables a modulo-6 counter for the tens digit. The reset clears both digits, while the enable input is currently unused.

This module implements a Hamming(7,4) helper that either encodes four data bits into three parity bits or decodes seven received bits into a three-bit error syndrome for LED display. Its inputs are `enc`, an encode/decode select, and `data[7:1]`; its output is `pout[3:1]`. When `enc` is high, the output is set to XOR combinations of data bits 3, 5, 6, and 7 to produce parity bits. When `enc` is low, it instead forms the syndrome from XOR combinations of all seven data bits. The outputs update when `enc` changes.

This module implements a two-input logical AND gate. It has two 1-bit inputs, x and y, and one 1-bit output, z. Internally, the output is continuously driven by the logical AND of the two inputs, so z is high only when both x and y are high.

Coordinates double-buffered data transfer between a producer and consumer. Inputs are ready_p, ack_p, and clk; outputs are enable_p, irq_p, and bank_p. A clocked edge detector watches ack_p for a rising edge. The irq_p register sets when ready_p is high and clears on an ack rise, while bank_p toggles when ready_p is high and irq_p is low. enable_p is held low.

This module implements a 4-to-1 digital multiplexer. It has four single-bit data inputs w, x, y, and z, a 2-bit select input s, and a single-bit output F. The internal logic is purely combinational: F follows w, x, y, or z depending on whether s equals 00, 01, 10, or 11, respectively. No clock or state is involved.

This module implements a secondary address decoder that determines whether a selected secondary address is enabled. Its inputs are a 32-bit secondary-address mask and a 5-bit data input index, DI; its single output is the one-bit secAddrDetected flag. Internally, it is purely combinational, using DI to select the corresponding bit from the mask and driving that bit directly to the output. Thus, the output reflects whether the mask bit at position DI is set.

This module drives a serial trigger output interface, producing a 100 MHz differential clock and an 800 Mbps differential data stream. Its inputs are 100 MHz and 400 MHz clocks, an asynchronous reset, an 8-bit TRIG_TX value, and TRIG_VALID; outputs are differential TRIG_CLKP/N and TRIG_DATP/N. Two SEROUT8 serializers generate the outputs: one sends a fixed 0xF0 clock pattern, while the other sends the trigger byte LSB-first. TRIG_TX and TRIG_VALID are registered on CLK_100MHZ. The serialized data is all ones when TRIG_VALID is low, otherwise it is the registered trigger byte.

This module implements a 4-bit carry-lookahead adder that can also perform subtraction by conditionally inverting operand B. Its inputs are 4-bit A and B plus carry-in Cin; outputs are 4-bit Sum and carry-out Cout. Internally, each B bit is XORed with Cin to form Bxor. A carry-lookahead logic block computes the internal carry bits from A, Bxor, and Cin, and four 1-bit full adders generate Sum. Cout comes from the lookahead block, and the full adders' carry outputs are unused.

This module is a synchronous 2-to-1 multiplexer for 24-bit RGB888 pixel data. It has a clock input, a select input, two 24-bit data inputs, and one 24-bit registered output. On each rising clock edge, the output captures the first input when select is low, or the second input when select is high. The selection is therefore aligned to the clock, with no reset or other control logic.
Response:
module rgb888_mux_2(
input wire clk,
input wire sel,
input wire [23:0] rgb888_0,
input wire [23:0] rgb888_1,
output reg [23:0] rgb888
);
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if(sel == 1'b0) begin
      rgb888 <= rgb888_0;
    end
    else begin
      rgb888 <= rgb888_1;
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module drives three independent LED blinkers, one per clock domain. It takes three clock inputs (clk_i, clk2_i, clk3_i) and an active-low reset rst_n_i, and outputs a 3-bit LED bus leds_o. The reset is inverted internally to an active-high signal. Three Blink instances, each parameterized for a 50 MHz clock, generate separate blink waveforms from their respective clocks. These three blink outputs are concatenated into leds_o, with the first instance on bit 0 and the third on bit 2.
Response:
module Top(
input wire clk_i,
input wire clk2_i,
input wire clk3_i,
input wire rst_n_i,
output wire [2:0] leds_o
);
wire rst; wire led0; wire led1; wire led2;
  assign rst =  ~rst_n_i;
  Blink #(
      .FREQUENCY(50e6))
  blink0prog_inst(
      .clk_i(clk_i),
    .rst_i(rst),
    .blink_o(led0));
  Blink #(
      .FREQUENCY(50e6))
  blink1prog_inst(
      .clk_i(clk2_i),
    .rst_i(rst),
    .blink_o(led1));
  Blink #(
      .FREQUENCY(50e6))
  blink2prog_inst(
      .clk_i(clk3_i),
    .rst_i(rst),
    .blink_o(led2));
  assign leds_o = {led2,led1,led0};
endmodule

Instruction: This module is a synchronous program-counter controller for instruction/opcode fetch. Its inputs are CLK_I, T2, CLR, CE, a 3-bit PC_OP select, and data buses JDATA, RR, and RDATA; its 16-bit PC output directly reflects the internal LPC register. On each rising clock edge LPC is cleared to zero when CLR is high, otherwise when CE and T2 are both high, PC_OP selects the update: increment, jump, return-address handling via LRET, register jump, hold, or a default interrupt vector.

ucecho is a clocked 8-bit echo and character-case converter. It has an 8-bit data input pd, an 8-bit data output pb, and a clock input fxclk. An internal register continuously drives pb and captures pd on each rising clock edge. If the captured value is a lowercase ASCII letter (decimal 97–122), 32 is subtracted to produce the corresponding uppercase code. All other input values pass through unchanged, and the design has no reset.

This module is a 16-bit-wide 2-to-1 multiplexer. It has two 16-bit data inputs, `a` and `b`, a 1-bit select input `sel`, and a 16-bit output `y`. When `sel` is 0, `y` outputs `a`; when `sel` is 1, `y` outputs `b`. Internally, a generate loop creates one combinational bitwise select per bit, using AND-OR logic to choose between corresponding bits of `a` and `b`.

This module implements a four-state finite state machine that generates a scanning anode signal, likely for a multiplexed seven-segment display. It has a clock and reset input and a 4-bit `anode_o` output. The FSM cycles through four states (`an3`, `an2`, `an1`, `an0`); in each non-reset state it drives one anode line low while the other three remain high. Asserting reset returns the FSM to the initial `an3` state. The state register advances on the clock, and it also has an unusual asynchronous sensitivity to its own rising edge.

RegistrosMemoria is a top-level wrapper for a processor’s register/memory subsystem, integrating upper and lower register banks. It takes a clock, reset, a 25-bit control word, memory/ALU flags, an 8-bit data-bus input, and an 8-bit ALU result; it outputs 8-bit IR and MBR values plus 12-bit AR and IP. Internally, the upper block manages AR, IP, and the IR/MBR path, while the lower block handles ALU-result and data-bus transfers. Shared 8-bit IR/MBR wires connect the two submodules and drive the module outputs.
Response:
module RegistrosMemoria(
input wire clk,
input wire ma,
input wire me,
input wire z,
input wire [7:0] bus_datos_out,
input wire [7:0] alu_sal,
input wire senal_rst,
input wire [24:0] control,
output wire [7:0] ir_sal,
output wire [7:0] mbr_sal,
output wire [11:0] ar_sal,
output wire [11:0] salida_ip
);
wire [7:0] ir_sal_gay; wire [7:0] mbr_sal_gay;
  assign ir_sal = ir_sal_gay;
  assign mbr_sal = mbr_sal_gay;
  RegistrosArriba arriba(

    me,
    z,
    ma,
    control,

    senal_rst,
