Instruction: This module computes twice its input, treating the 8-bit input as a signed value. It has an 8-bit input `data_in` and an 11-bit output `data_out`. Internally, the input is shifted left by one bit, with the lowest output bit set to zero, forming the lower nine bits of the result. The input’s most-significant bit is copied into the top two output bits to sign-extend the doubled value to 11 bits. The design is purely combinational.

This module, cmp_138, is a 3-bit equality comparator. It takes two 3-bit inputs, in0 and in1, and produces a single 1-bit output, eq. Internally, it compares the two inputs and drives eq high when they are equal, otherwise low. An intermediate wire holds the comparison result before it is assigned to eq.

This module, C2, is a purely combinational 4-bit bitwise OR gate. It receives two 4-bit input vectors, A and B, and produces a 4-bit output vector, F. Each bit of F is the logical OR of the corresponding bits of A and B. There is no clock or stored state; F updates continuously as A or B changes.

This module implements a combinational two-input XNOR logic gate. It has two 1-bit inputs, A and B, and one 1-bit output, Z. Internally, Z is assigned the logical complement of A XOR B, so it is high when A and B are equal and low when they differ.

This module is a clock divider that derives two slow periodic pulse signals from a fast input clock. Its ports are an input `clock`, an active-low asynchronous `reset`, and outputs `c1` and `c2`. Two independent 32-bit counters run on each rising clock edge: the first emits a one-cycle-high pulse on `c1` every 50,000,000 cycles (1 Hz at 50 MHz), and the second emits a pulse on `c2` every 12,500,000 cycles (4 Hz). Both counters clear to zero on reset or upon reaching their terminal count.

This module implements a 7:1 SerDes differential receiver that deserializes six LVDS data channels using a clock recovered from a differential reference clock. Inputs are an active-high reset, a differential clock pair, and six differential data pairs; the output is a registered 42-bit bus. Internally, a clock-recovery PLL submodule generates the serialization strobe, bitslip, and buffered clock, while a data submodule deserializes the six lanes into the wide bus. The deserialized data is captured into the output register on each rising edge of the recovered clock.

This module implements a four-state Mealy finite state machine that tracks runs of consecutive high bits on a serial input. It has a clock, an asynchronous active-high reset, a one-bit serial data input, and a two-bit registered output. On each rising clock edge the state advances from s0 through s3 on consecutive high inputs, stays in s3 on further highs, and moves back to an earlier state when the input goes low. Reset forces the state to s0. The output is combinational, decoded from the current state and input without waiting for a clock edge.
Response:
module mealy_4s(
input wire clk,
input wire data_in,
input wire reset,
output reg [1:0] data_out
);
// Build an enumerated type for the state machine
parameter [1:0]
  s0 = 0,
  s1 = 1,
  s2 = 2,
  s3 = 3;
  // Register to hold the current state
reg [1:0] state;
  always @(posedge clk, posedge reset) begin
    if(reset == 1'b1) begin
      state <= s0;
    end else begin
      // Determine the next state synchronously, based on
      // the current state and the input
      case(state)
      s0 : begin
        if(data_in == 1'b1) begin
          state <= s1;
        end
        else begin
          state <= s0;
        end
      end
      s1 : begin
        if(data_in == 1'b1) begin
          state <= s2;
        end
        else begin
          state <= s1;
        end
      end
      s2 : begin
        if(data_in == 1'b1) begin
          state <= s3;
        end
        else begin
          state <= s2;
        end
      end
      s3 : begin
        if(data_in == 1'b1) begin
          state <= s3;
        end
        else begin
          state <= s1;
        end
      end
      endcase
    end
  end
  // Determine the output based only on the current state
  // and the input (do not wait for a clock edge).
  always @(state, data_in) begin
    case(state)
    s0 : begin
      if(data_in == 1'b1) begin
        data_out <= 2'b00;
      end
      else begin
        data_out <= 2'b01;
      end
    end
    s1 : begin
      if(data_in == 1'b1) begin
        data_out <= 2'b01;
      end
      else begin
        data_out <= 2'b11;
      end
    end
    s2 : begin
      if(data_in == 1'b1) begin
        data_out <= 2'b10;
      end
      else begin
        data_out <= 2'b10;
      end
    end
    s3 : begin
      if(data_in == 1'b1) begin
        data_out <= 2'b11;
      end
      else begin
        data_out <= 2'b10;
      end
    end
    endcase
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module is a 3-bit 2-to-1 multiplexer that selects between two 3-bit inputs based on a single control signal. Its ports are a one-bit SELECTOR input, two 3-bit data inputs named JUEGO and SWITCH, and a 3-bit output named DISPLAY. Internally, combinational logic continuously evaluates SELECTOR: when it is high, DISPLAY follows JUEGO; when low, DISPLAY follows SWITCH. An unreachable default case assigns an unknown 3-bit value. The design has no clock or state, so the output changes immediately with its inputs.

This module implements the top-level datapath/control for a simple MIPS-style processor, coordinating instruction fetch, decode, execute, and memory access stages. Its inputs are the fetched instruction, clock, reset, memory read data, and a memory-read qualifier; its outputs are the next program counter, fetch enable, memory address, memory read/write strobes, and memory write data. Internally it instantiates a decoder, sign extender, ALU, PC/branch bridge, memory read-write unit, and next-PC logic, with a clock counter that does not affect datapath control. Stall/pause and reset signals gate PC updates and instruction fetch, while the ALU and bridge generate branch/jump decisions and the memory stage drives external memory signals.

The module detects I2C START and STOP bus conditions. Its inputs are clk_i, active-low rst_n_i, serial data/clock lines input_sda_i/input_scl_i, and start_ack_i/stop_ack_i; outputs are start_state_o and stop_state_o flags. Two independent three-state finite-state machines monitor SDA while SCL is high: one flags a START when SDA falls after both lines are idle high, and the other flags a STOP when SDA rises after SCL is high with SDA low. Each flag remains asserted until its matching ACK is received, then returns to idle; reset clears both flags.

This module is a quadrature rotary-encoder decoder that converts the A and B phase inputs into direction pulses. It has a clock input, encoder inputs A and B, and registered outputs inc and dec. Internally, two-stage registers sample and delay A and B each clock cycle, then detect transitions on either channel. Depending on the level of the other channel at each edge, it asserts inc or dec for one clock, or leaves both low when no edge occurs.

The demo module drives four LEDs from buttons, DIP switches, clock, reset, and header pins. Inputs are 4-bit button and DIP-switch buses, clock, and reset; output is a 4-bit LED bus, plus a 4-bit bidirectional header bus. A clock divider generates a 2 Hz clock from the input clock. An inverter submodule derives LED0 and LED1 from button[0], while a blink submodule toggles LED2 when enabled by dip_sw[0] at 2 Hz. LED3 is asserted only when all buttons, DIP switches, clock, reset, and header bits are high.

This module implements a simple two-input OR gate. It has two 1-bit inputs, x and y, and one 1-bit output, z. Internally, the output is continuously driven by the logical OR of the two inputs. Therefore, z is high whenever either input is high, and low only when both inputs are low. The design is purely combinational and has no stored state.

This top-level module drives an LED blinker whose speed is set by two pushbuttons. Inputs are an active-low reset, a clock, and two active-low buttons; outputs are the LED (active high) and a 3-bit frequency code (000 stops blinking, 111 is fastest). Internally it instantiates a `freq_controller` that adjusts the frequency code from button presses and a `ledblinker` that flashes the LED at that rate. Both submodules share the same 3-bit `freq_tmp` signal, which is also routed to the `freq` output.

This module generates VGA color signals forming eight vertical color bars. Its inputs are an enable, 32-bit horizontal (Xin) and vertical (Yin) pixel coordinates; outputs are 3-bit red, 3-bit green, and 2-bit blue. When enabled, an 8-bit color is selected based on which 80-pixel-wide horizontal band Xin falls into, each band having a distinct color; when disabled the output is black. The selected color byte is split into red, green, and blue fields. Timing parameters are declared, but Yin is unused.

This module implements a simple combinational connection between a button input and an LED output. It has one single-bit input named button and one single-bit output named LED. The output directly follows the input at all times, with no clock or sequential elements. No other logic or state is present, so the LED immediately reflects the button signal.

This module is a 10-input, 10-output finite state machine built around a reconfigurable TRFSM core with a 5-bit state register. It has an active-low reset, a clock, ten data inputs, ten registered outputs, and a serial configuration interface (mode, clock, shift, data in/out). Internally it packs the inputs into a 10-bit vector for the core, unpacks the core's 10-bit output to the output pins, and ties the unused scan chain signals low. The core is configured with five rows per state group.

Instruction: This module is a 32-bit register with byte-slice write capability, clocked by clk and synchronously cleared when rst_n is low. Its inputs are clk, rst_n, a 2-bit write address, 8-bit data and mask, and a valid flag; outputs are the registered 32-bit value and an always-asserted read strobe. Internally, a combinational next value is formed; address 2'b01 loads the input byte into bits 15:8 while preserving other slices, otherwise slices default to 0x7B, 0x00, and 0x0000. The mask and valid inputs are unused.

The ADD module is a purely combinational 32-bit adder. It has two 32-bit inputs, IN_A and IN_B, and one 32-bit output, OUT_A. Internally, OUT_A is continuously assigned the arithmetic sum of IN_A and IN_B. The output updates immediately whenever either input changes, with no clock or storage involved.

This module generates one Booth-encoded partial product for a 16-bit multiplicand. Its inputs are the 3-bit multiplier triplet `bin3` and the 16-bit multiplicand `a`; its output is a 17-bit partial product. Combinational logic selects +a, +2a, -a, -2a, or zero depending on `bin3`, with negation performed via two's complement. The block is sensitive to both inputs.

This module acts as a VME DMA arbiter between slave and master requesters. It has a clock and async reset, slave/master request inputs, slave/master acknowledge outputs, and a slave-arbitration output. Internally, the slave acknowledge and arbitration select are always deasserted, so slave requests are never granted. The master acknowledge is simply the master request delayed one clock, cleared asynchronously on reset.

This module is a pipeline register that carries execution-stage signals into the memory stage. Its inputs are CLK, RESET, and EX-stage control/datapath signals: memory/register write enables, MemToReg, MemRead, OVF, Zero, MULDIV, two ALU results, Data2, and the register write address. Its outputs are the matching MEM-stage versions of those signals. On each rising clock edge the inputs are latched to the outputs; an asynchronous active-high RESET clears all outputs to zero.

This module is a 27-bit adder that outputs the sum of two 27-bit inputs, discarding any final carry-out. It has one 27-bit output, result, and two 27-bit inputs, in_a and in_b. Internally, it widens both inputs into 29-bit values: in_a has a constant 1 appended as its least significant bit, while in_b has a 0 appended. The two widened values are added, and bits 27 down to 1 of the sum are assigned to result, so the appended constant is effectively discarded and the result equals (in_a + in_b) modulo 2^27.

This module is a top-level pipelined MIPS processor. It outputs the 32-bit program counter (pc) and current instruction (instr), and takes a clock (clk), reset, and a dump control input. Internally it instantiates a controller, which decodes the opcode and funct fields into control signals (ALU control, register write, memory write, branch, jump, etc.), and a datapath, which executes instructions and generates pc, instr, and the datapath signals. The instr output is driven directly from the datapath's instruction value.
Response:
module pipeline(
output wire [31:0] pc,
output wire [31:0] instr,
input wire dump,
input wire reset,
input wire clk
);
//DECLARACION DE COMPONENTES--
//DECLARACION DE SEniALES--

wire [2:0] AluControl_s;

  controller CONTROLLER1(
      .Op(Instr_s[31:26]),
    .Funct(Instr_s[5:0]),
    .MemToReg(MemToReg_s),
    .MemWrite(MemWrite_s),

    .AluSrc(AluSrc_s),
    .RegDst(RegDst_s),

  datapath DATAPATH1(
      .MemToReg(MemToReg_s),
    .MemWrite(MemWrite_s),
    .Branch(Branch_s),
    .AluSrc(AluSrc_s),
    .RegDst(RegDst_s),
    .RegWrite(RegWrite_s),
    .Jump(Jump_s),
    .AluControl(AluControl_s),
    .dump(dump),
    .pc(pc),
    .instr(Instr_s),
    .reset(reset),
    .clk(clk));
  assign instr = Instr_s;
    // IMPORTANTE !!!
endmodule

Instruction: This module is a 20-bit unsigned adder that outputs the low 20 bits of the sum of its two inputs, ignoring any carry out. It has a 20-bit output `result` and two 20-bit inputs, `in_a` and `in_b`. Internally, each input is widened with a leading zero and an appended constant bit: `in_a` gets a trailing 1 and `in_b` a trailing 0. The widened values are added, and bits [20:1] of the sum are selected as the result. The appended bit only affects the discarded LSB, so the output equals `in_a + in_b` modulo 2^20.

This module divides a 50 MHz input clock down to a 0.0625 Hz square wave. It has an active-high asynchronous reset, a clock input, and a single clock output. A 32-bit counter increments on each input clock edge; when it reaches 399,999,999, the output register toggles and the counter resets. Asserting reset clears both the counter and the output, resulting in a 50% duty-cycle output.

This module implements a clocked, address-decoded 32-bit register that can be read or written through a bidirectional data bus. It has a 32-bit inout databus, a 16-bit addressbus, 32-bit info and registerbits, plus write, read, and clock inputs; an address parameter selects the register. On each rising clock edge, the internal register is cleared, then only when the address matches it latches the databus on a write or drives info onto the databus on a read. Otherwise the databus is left high-impedance, and registerbits continuously outputs the stored value.

This module implements a 32-bit adder that computes the sum of two 32-bit inputs, discarding any carry beyond bit 31. It has a 32-bit output `result` and two 32-bit inputs `in_a` and `in_b`. Internally, it forms two 34-bit values by zero-padding each input and appending a low bit (1 for `in_a`, 0 for `in_b`). These are added to produce a 34-bit sum, and bits 32 down to 1 of that sum become `result`. The padding and extra low bit do not affect the final 32-bit sum.

Converts an 8-bit two's-complement value into its unsigned magnitude and presents it as two 4-bit hexadecimal nibbles. The inputs are the 8-bit `in_string`; outputs are `out1` (high nibble) and `out0` (low nibble). Internally, the sign bit is tested: non-negative values pass through unchanged, while negative values are negated using two's complement. The resulting magnitude is split into upper and lower 4-bit halves, and the outputs update whenever the input changes.

MX_5 is a 32-bit 2:1 multiplexer. It has a 1-bit control input `MemtoReg`, two 32-bit data inputs `IN_A` and `IN_B`, and a 32-bit output `OUT_A`. When `MemtoReg` is low, `OUT_A` follows `IN_B`; when high, `OUT_A` follows `IN_A`. The selection is implemented as a continuous conditional assignment.

This module is a 32-bit adder/subtractor with a registered output. It takes inputs sysclk, reset, enable, addsub, and two 32-bit operands aa and bb, producing a 32-bit result cc. Internally, addsub is XORed with each bit of bb and injected as a carry-in, so the same adder performs addition when addsub is low and subtraction when high. The result is captured in a 32-bit register on each rising clock edge only when enable is asserted, and is cleared asynchronously when reset is high.

This module implements a small microcontroller system around a kcpsm3 CPU that controls serial communication, LEDs, a pushbutton input, and timer-driven interrupt events. Its inputs are reset, clock, button, and serial receive; its outputs are serial transmit, two event signals (interrupt and RETURNI), and two LED controls. Internally it synchronizes the reset, button, and receive signals to the system clock, instantiates the CPU, program ROM, and timer, and uses a port decoder to generate write enables and read-data selection. Writes to specific ports drive the LEDs and serial transmit line through clocked flip-flops, while reads return button/LED status and the synchronized serial input. The timer supplies the interrupt request and acknowledge signals for the CPU.

This module is the top-level FPGA controller for an RGB LED display system that can show either received UART data or generated animations. Its ports include clocks, PLL lock, UART active, height/mode/on-off controls, serial TX/RX lines, and display panel outputs for RGB data, addressing, clock, output-enable, and latch. Internally, a UART receiver captures serial input, an animation block generates display data, and a multiplexer selects between UART and animation data based on the uart_active signal. The selected data is fed to a display controller that drives the panel, while the reset is derived from the PLL lock and unused serial outputs are tied high.

This module is intended to sign-extend a 30-bit value to 32 bits. It takes a 30-bit input, `Disp30`, and produces a 32-bit output, `SEU_Disp30_Out`. Internally, bit 21 of the input acts as the sign bit: if it is 0, the two upper output bits are set to 00; otherwise they are set to 11, with the lower 30 bits copied from the input. Note that the code assigns a differently-cased internal signal inside an `always` block to a wire output, so it may not correctly drive the declared port in standard Verilog.

This module is a simple constant-zero, or ground, source. It has one 1-bit output port and no inputs. Internally, it continuously drives that output to logic low. It is typically used to provide a fixed 0 value or tie-off to downstream logic.

This module is a top-level wrapper for a LED chaser (chenillard) design. Its ports include a clock input, an active-high reset tied low internally, three 16-bit bidirectional buses, a serial receive input, and a bidirectional transmit line, though only one bus bit is used as a button input and four others drive LEDs. Internally, a 24-bit counter divides the main clock, using its most significant bit as a slow clock for the chaser instance. Most remaining I/O and the reset are unused in this top level.

This module is a configurable down-counter that generates a tick pulse. Its inputs are clk, reset, count-enable T, and selection bits E2–E0; its output S indicates the counter has reached zero. A two-state FSM alternately loads a selected initial count and then counts down on T pulses. When the count hits zero, S goes high and the FSM reloads the starting value. The initial count is chosen from 2 to 20 by the E2–E0 value.

This module is an up counter that asserts a trigger when its count reaches zero. Its inputs are clk, rst, and a 16-bit rst_val; its only output is trigger. A 22-bit internal register is asynchronously loaded with rst_val when rst is high, and otherwise increments on each rising clk edge. The trigger output is high only while the counter value equals zero.

This module implements a basic two-input AND gate. It has two single-bit inputs, A and B, and one single-bit output, C. The output is driven combinationally from the logical AND of the two inputs. There are no clocked elements, resets, or state storage.

This module implements a simple UART transmitter. It accepts a clock, asynchronous reset, 8-bit data input, and a write strobe, and outputs a busy flag and serial transmit line. A parameter defines the bit period, with half-bit timing derived internally. When idle and write is asserted, it loads the data, sends a start bit, shifts out eight data bits LSB-first at the configured rate, then sends a stop bit while busy is high.

This module is a single-bit D flip-flop with an intended asynchronous, active-low reset. Its ports are i_Clock, i_Reset_n, i_D as data input, and o_Q as the registered output. On each rising clock edge, the internal register Q loads i_D, and o_Q is driven directly from that register. Because the always block is sensitive to a rising edge of i_Reset_n while testing for a low level, the intended asynchronous clear does not actually take effect.

This module is a 39-bit unsigned adder that produces the truncated sum of two 39-bit operands. Its ports are two 39-bit inputs, in_a and in_b, and a 39-bit output, output. Internally, each input is zero-extended to 41 bits and concatenated with a constant low bit (1 for in_a, 0 for in_b), effectively doubling the operand values before adding them in a 41-bit sum. The output is the middle slice of that sum, so the appended low bit and any final carry-out are discarded, yielding in_a + in_b with overflow dropped.

This module is a 32-bit ALU that produces a result selected by a 6-bit operation code. Its inputs are the two 32-bit operands ope1 and ope2, the 6-bit aluop select, and a carry input; the output is the 32-bit result alurs. Internal combinational case logic implements addition, add-with-carry, subtraction, subtract-with-borrow, and bitwise AND, NAND, OR, NOR, XOR, and XNOR. Some consecutive opcodes perform the same operation (with/without condition-code updates), and any unrecognized opcode returns zero.

This module bridges a 6-bit GPIO interface to an LCD controller, letting an external host reset the display, set the cursor position, and write characters. Inputs are rst, clk, and gpio[5:0]; outputs are LCD control signals lcd_en/rw/rs/bl and bidirectional 4-bit lcd_data. Inside, an FSM samples gpio[5] as a clock and uses gpio[4:0] as command/payload, sequencing through idle, character-high, character-low, and position states. An LCD submodule drives the display; the logic latches character/position and pulses flush when the LCD is ready, with reset/reinit handling.

This module wraps an external-memory example design with built-in stimulus generation and data checking. It takes CLK_IN and RESET_IN inputs and produces a 9-bit STATUS output. A three-stage synchronizer generates an internal reset, while a stimulus generator drives write, address, and data signals into the memory port through delayed registers. A checker monitors memory read data and accumulates error flags into STATUS[7:0], and STATUS[8] reflects a delayed write-activity counter bit.

This module is a simple constant signal generator that drives a 4-bit output to a fixed binary pattern. Its only port is `M`, a 4-bit output bus. Internally, the module uses a continuous assignment to permanently set `M` to `4'b0101`, meaning bits 3 and 1 are high while bits 2 and 0 are low. There are no inputs, clocks, or other logic, so the output never changes.

transceiver_test is a test harness for a transceiver transmit datapath, driving a serial output pair from switch/status inputs. Ports include clk, switches, leds, debug_pmod, differential refclocks, high-speed outputs gtptxp/n, and DisplayPort-style aux/hot-plug-detect signals. Internally, a symbol clock feeds a pattern source, scrambler, training/channel-delay block, and 8b/10b encoder that produce two symbol streams for the transceiver. A management clock register enables all four powerup channels; most configuration/status signals and data are tied off to constants.

The module performs bitwise exclusive-OR (modulo-2 addition) on two 3-bit vectors. It has two 3-bit inputs, `a` and `b`, and one 3-bit output, `c`. Each output bit is computed independently as the XOR of the corresponding input bits. There is no carry, borrow, or interaction between bit positions.

The module is named adder but does not perform addition; it effectively implements a 2:1 multiplexer. Inputs are A, B, C, and carryIn; outputs are carryOut, fnord, and registered sum. Internally, an always block sensitive only to A sets sum to B when A is 0 and to C when A is 1. Input carryIn and outputs carryOut/fnord are never used or driven. Because B and C are missing from the sensitivity list, sum updates only when A changes, so it is not fully combinational.
Response:
module adder(
input wire A,
input wire B,
input wire C,
input wire carryIn,
output wire carryOut,
output wire fnord,
output reg sum
);
  always @(A) begin
    case(A)
    1'b0 : begin
      case(B)
      1'b0 : begin
        sum <= 1'b0;
      end
      1'b1 : begin
        sum <= 1'b1;
      end
      endcase
    end
    1'b1 : begin
      case(C)
      1'b0 : begin
        sum <= 1'b0;
      end
      1'b1 : begin
        sum <= 1'b1;
      end
      endcase
    end
    endcase
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module implements an HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor interface. Its inputs are CLOCK_CORE, INIT_KEY, and ECHO; its outputs are TRIGGER and a 32-bit DIST bus. An internal divider toggles hc_clock every COUNT_MAX clock cycles to create a slower timing clock. A state machine enabled by INIT_KEY is intended to pulse TRIGGER, count the ECHO-high duration, and compute distance into dist_mm. However, the state machine does not transition as written and DIST is never driven, so no valid external distance output is produced.

`round_f` computes one round of a 128-bit ARIA-like block cipher, processing four 32-bit state words. Its inputs include `clk`, `rst`, direction select `enc`, round constant `rc_in`, state words `a_0_in`–`a_3_in`, and round-key words `k_0_in`–`k_3_in`; outputs are four 32-bit words `a_0_out`–`a_3_out`. Internally it performs optional round-constant XOR (before the theta stage for decryption, after the first register stage for encryption), theta key mixing, two clocked pipeline stages, byte permutations `pi_1` and `pi_2`, and gamma S-box substitution. The `enc` signal controls where the round constant is injected.

This module implements a single AES-style AddRoundKey step, XORing a 32-bit input word with a 32-bit round key. It has a clock, reset, two 32-bit inputs (`wordIn`, `keyIn`), and a registered 32-bit output (`wordOut`). On reset, the output is cleared to zero; otherwise it stores the bitwise XOR of the two inputs. The always block is sensitive to clock, reset, and rising edges of both data inputs, so the output can also update asynchronously when an input rises.
Response:
module addRoundKey(
input wire CLK,
input wire RESET,
input wire [31:0] wordIn,
input wire [31:0] keyIn,
output reg [31:0] wordOut
);
  always @(posedge CLK, posedge RESET, posedge wordIn, posedge keyIn) begin
    if(RESET == 1'b1) begin
      wordOut <= {32{1'b0}};
    end else begin
      wordOut <= wordIn ^ keyIn;
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This top-level module implements an SPI master controller that transmits a fixed byte and receives one byte over a serial bus. Its inputs are a 50 MHz clock, a start trigger, and MISO; its outputs are the received 8-bit data, a done flag, MOSI, chip select, and SPI clock. Internally it instantiates an SPI master configured for 10 MHz, 8-bit transfers, CPOL=1, CPHA=0, and transmit data 0xAE. A small internal bus maps the SPI signals to the external pins.

This module implements a simple storage element intended as a D latch: it captures the data input when the clock is high and otherwise holds its previous value. It has two 1-bit inputs, `clk` and `d`, and one 1-bit registered output, `q`. Internally, an always block triggered by changes on `clk` assigns `d` to `q` when `clk` is high; otherwise `q` retains its prior value. Because the block is sensitive only to `clk`, changes on `d` while `clk` remains high are not captured, so it behaves more like a clock-triggered register than a fully transparent latch. No reset or enable input is provided.
Response:
module Latch(
input wire clk,
input wire d,
output reg q
);
  always @(clk) begin
    if((clk == 1'b1)) begin
      q <= d;
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module performs a 32-bit subtraction, producing result = in_a minus in_b. It has a 32-bit output named result and two 32-bit inputs, in_a and in_b. Internally, each input is zero-extended and shifted to form 34-bit intermediate values, which are subtracted. The lower intermediate bit is dropped, and bits 32 down to 1 of the difference become the output.

This module is a 1024×32-bit single-port RAM with a registered read path. Inputs are clk, active-high chip select cs, read, write, a 10-bit address, and 32-bit wrdata; output is 32-bit rddata. On each clock edge it registers the address and a read-enable derived from cs and read, while synchronous writes store wrdata when cs and write are both high. The read output is combinational from the registered address when the registered read-enable is active, otherwise it is high-impedance.

PMem implements a 4K×16 program memory using four 2K×8 SRAM blocks. It has active-low reset and chip enable, a clock, 12-bit address, 16-bit write data, 2-bit byte-write enable, and registered 16-bit read data. Address bit 11 selects one of two 2K×16 banks, each built from two byte-wide SRAMs. Clock-gated logic generates the per-block chip-enable and write-enable signals. On a clock edge, when enabled, the selected bank’s data is latched to the output; reset clears it.

This module implements a parameterized N-stage enabled shift register/delay line. It has inputs clock, reset, enable, and serial data D, and output Q. Internally it chains N flip-flop stages, with D feeding the first stage and each stage feeding the next. The last stage’s output drives Q, so Q is D delayed by N enabled clock cycles. The delay depth is set by parameter N, defaulting to 1.

This module handles SpaceWire time-code reception for a CODEC IP. Its inputs are the system clock, reset, receive clock, a time-code-received strobe, and an 8-bit received time code; outputs are a 6-bit time value, 2-bit control flags, and a tick pulse. A one-pulse synchronizer moves the strobe into the system clock domain. On each synchronized strobe, the input byte is split into control flags (top bits) and time value (low six bits), and the tick asserts when the new value equals the previous time value plus one. Reset clears all registers and outputs.

This module implements a five-digit BCD adder. It takes two 20-bit BCD operands (Entrada1 and Entrada2), each containing five 4-bit decimal digits, and outputs a 20-bit BCD sum plus a 4-bit carry. Internally, five single-digit BCD adder submodules are cascaded: each stage adds one digit pair with a carry-in, producing a digit result and carry-out. The carry propagates from the least-significant to the most-significant digit, and the final carry-out drives the carry output.

FREQDIV is a clock frequency divider that produces an output clock at 1/2^20 of the input clock frequency. It has one input, CLK, and one output, CLK2. Internally, a 20-bit counter increments on every rising edge of CLK. The output CLK2 is driven directly by the counter’s most significant bit, giving a 50% duty-cycle divided clock. The module has no reset or other control logic.

This module is a VGA video generator producing a 512x768 display from external VRAM. Its inputs are the pixel clock, active-low reset, VRAM read data, a 7-bit palette (COLORS), plus HI_RES and BLANK_SCR controls; outputs are a 14-bit VRAM address, 4-bit R/G/B, and HSYNC/VSYNC. Horizontal and vertical counters generate sync timing and the active (paper) window, while a row counter and three-row counter step through VRAM addresses. Latched pixels are expanded per resolution mode, mapped through a palette mux to RGB, and repeated over three scanlines (dimmed on outer rows), with output blanked outside the visible area.

This module generates a slow refresh clock by dividing the input oscillator frequency. It has an asynchronous reset input Rst, a clock input Clk, and a registered output ClkOut. Parameters Fosc and Fdiv define the division ratio, so an internal counter counts Clk cycles up to Fosc/Fdiv. When that terminal count is reached, the counter resets and ClkOut pulses high for one cycle; otherwise ClkOut stays low. Rst asynchronously clears the counter.

RD_Mux is a combinational 6-bit multiplexer that selects the read-destination register code. Its inputs are the 1-bit select signal RfDest and the 6-bit index RD; its output is the 6-bit nRD. When RfDest is high, nRD is forced to the fixed value 15 (six-bit 001111); otherwise nRD follows RD. The output updates whenever either input changes.
Response:
module RD_Mux(
input wire RfDest,
input wire [5:0] RD,
output reg [5:0] nRD
);
  always @(RfDest, RD) begin
    if((RfDest == 1'b1)) begin
      nRD <= 6'b001111;
    end
    else begin
      nRD <= RD;
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: Two-state finite-state machine that arbitrates a data-transmission handshake. Inputs are clock, active-high asynchronous reseta, start request transmite_dado, and completion flag pronto; the registered output trans_andamento indicates an active transfer. It starts in inicial and advances to transmissao when transmite_dado is asserted. It returns to inicial once pronto is high, and reset forces inicial. The output is 0 during inicial and 1 during transmissao.
Response:
module interface_trans_uc(
input wire clock,
input wire reseta,
input wire transmite_dado,
input wire pronto,
output reg trans_andamento
);
parameter [0:0]
  inicial = 0,
  transmissao = 1;
reg estado;
  always @(posedge clock, posedge estado, posedge reseta) begin
    if(reseta == 1'b1) begin
      estado <= inicial;
    end else begin
      case(estado)
      inicial : begin
        // Aguarda sinal de inicio de transmissão
        if(transmite_dado == 1'b1) begin
          estado <= transmissao;
        end
        else begin
          estado <= inicial;
        end
      end
      transmissao : begin
        if(pronto == 1'b1) begin
          estado <= inicial;
        end
        else begin
          estado <= transmissao;
        end
      end
      endcase
    end
  end
  always @(estado) begin
    case(estado)
    inicial : begin
      trans_andamento <= 1'b0;
    end
    transmissao : begin
      trans_andamento <= 1'b1;
    end
    endcase
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module is a 16-bit two-input multiplexer that selects between a register value and the program counter to produce operand A. Its inputs are a 2-bit select alusrca, 16-bit muxreg1, and 16-bit mux_PC; the output is 16-bit mux_dataA. Internally, a case statement on alusrca drives mux_dataA: select value 0 chooses muxreg1, while value 1 chooses mux_PC. For any other select value, no assignment occurs, so mux_dataA retains its previous value.
Response:
module mux_reg1(
input wire [1:0] alusrca,
input wire [15:0] muxreg1,
input wire [15:0] mux_PC,
output reg [15:0] mux_dataA
);
  always @(alusrca) begin
    case(alusrca)
    2'b00 : begin
      mux_dataA <= muxreg1;
    end
    2'b01 : begin
      mux_dataA <= mux_PC;
    end
    default : begin
    end
    endcase
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module is the datapath of one AES decryption round core. It accepts CLK, RESET, memorySourceSelector, a 2-bit keySelector, a 128-bit cipherKey, and a 32-bit WORD_IN, producing a 32-bit WORD_OUT. Internally, the input word is buffered through memory units to build a 128-bit block, then inverse ShiftRows is applied. The result is further buffered and selected, inverse SubBytes is applied per byte, a round-key word chosen from cipherKey is added, and inverse MixColumns produces the output.
Response:
module decryptionLoopCore_V1(
input wire CLK,
input wire RESET,
input wire memorySourceSelector,
input wire [1:0] keySelector,
input wire [127:0] cipherKey,
input wire [31:0] WORD_IN,
output wire [31:0] WORD_OUT
);
wire [31:0] mu0_Out; wire [31:0] mu1_Out; wire [31:0] mu2_Out; wire [31:0] mu3_Out; wire [31:0] mu4_Out; wire [31:0] mu5_Out;
wire [31:0] invSubBytes_In; wire [31:0] invSubBytes_Out; reg [31:0] addRoundKey_KeyIn; wire [31:0] addRoundKey_Out;
wire [127:0] invShiftRows_In; wire [127:0] invShiftRows_Out;
wire ZERO_BIT = 1'b0;
wire [31:0] ZERO_WORD = 1'b0;
  assign ZERO_BIT = 1'b0;
  assign ZERO_WORD = {32{1'b0}};
  memoryUnit mu0(
      .CLK(CLK),
    .RESET(RESET),
    .SELB(ZERO_BIT),
    .wordAIn(WORD_IN),
    .wordBIn(ZERO_WORD),
    .wordOut(mu0_Out));
  memoryUnit mu1(
      .CLK(CLK),
    .RESET(RESET),
    .SELB(ZERO_BIT),
    .wordAIn(mu0_Out),
    .wordBIn(ZERO_WORD),
    .wordOut(mu1_Out));
  memoryUnit mu2(
      .CLK(CLK),
    .RESET(RESET),
    .SELB(ZERO_BIT),
    .wordAIn(mu1_Out),
    .wordBIn(ZERO_WORD),
    .wordOut(mu2_Out));
  assign invShiftRows_In = {mu2_Out,mu1_Out,mu0_Out,WORD_IN};
  invShiftRows invShiftRows0(
      .CLK(CLK),
    .RESET(RESET),
    .blockIn(invShiftRows_In),
    .blockOut(invShiftRows_Out));
  memoryUnit mu3(
      .CLK(CLK),
    .RESET(RESET),
    .SELB(memorySourceSelector),
    .wordAIn(invShiftRows_Out[31:0]),
    .wordBIn(invShiftRows_Out[31:0]),
    .wordOut(mu3_Out));
  memoryUnit mu4(
      .CLK(CLK),
    .RESET(RESET),
    .SELB(memorySourceSelector),
    .wordAIn(mu3_Out),
    .wordBIn(invShiftRows_Out[63:32]),
    .wordOut(mu4_Out));
  memoryUnit mu5(
      .CLK(CLK),
    .RESET(RESET),
    .SELB(memorySourceSelector),
    .wordAIn(mu4_Out),
    .wordBIn(invShiftRows_Out[95:64]),
    .wordOut(mu5_Out));
  assign invSubBytes_In = (memorySourceSelector == 1'b1) ? invShiftRows_Out[127:96] : mu5_Out;
  invSubByte invSubBytes0(
      .CLK(CLK),
    .RESET(RESET),
    .byteIn(invSubBytes_In[7:0]),
    .byteOut(invSubBytes_Out[7:0]));
  invSubByte invSubBytes1(
      .CLK(CLK),
    .RESET(RESET),
    .byteIn(invSubBytes_In[15:8]),
    .byteOut(invSubBytes_Out[15:8]));
  invSubByte invSubBytes2(
      .CLK(CLK),
    .RESET(RESET),
    .byteIn(invSubBytes_In[23:16]),
    .byteOut(invSubBytes_Out[23:16]));
  invSubByte invSubBytes3(
      .CLK(CLK),
    .RESET(RESET),
    .byteIn(invSubBytes_In[31:24]),
    .byteOut(invSubBytes_Out[31:24]));
  always @(cipherKey, keySelector) begin
    case(keySelector)
    2'b11 : begin
      addRoundKey_KeyIn <= cipherKey[127:96];
    end
    2'b10 : begin
      addRoundKey_KeyIn <= cipherKey[95:64];
    end
    2'b01 : begin
      addRoundKey_KeyIn <= cipherKey[63:32];
    end
    2'b00 : begin
      addRoundKey_KeyIn <= cipherKey[31:0];
    end
    default : begin
      addRoundKey_KeyIn <= {32{1'b0}};
    end
    endcase
  end
  addRoundKey addRoundKey0(
      .CLK(CLK),
    .RESET(RESET),
    .wordIn(invSubBytes_Out),
    .keyIn(addRoundKey_KeyIn),
    .wordOut(addRoundKey_Out));
  invMixColumn invMixColumn0(
      .CLK(CLK),
    .RESET(RESET),
    .wordIn(addRoundKey_Out),
    .wordOut(WORD_OUT));
endmodule

Instruction: This module is a combinational 32-bit adder that produces a truncated sum of its two inputs. It has 32-bit inputs in_a and in_b, plus a 32-bit output result. Internally, both inputs are widened to 34 bits: in_a gets a low-order 1 and in_b gets a low-order 0, then the widened values are added. Selecting bits 32 through 1 of that sum discards the added low bit and yields the 32-bit sum.

This module is a TMDS 8b/10b encoder, as used in DVI/HDMI links, converting each byte into a 10-bit DC-balanced serial symbol. It takes a clock, an 8-bit data byte, a 2-bit control input, and a blanking flag, and produces a registered 10-bit encoded output. Internally it builds both XOR- and XNOR-based transition-minimized words, counts the input's set bits to choose between them, and maintains a running DC bias that selects whether to invert the chosen word and which disparity bit to prepend. When blanking is asserted, it instead emits one of four fixed control symbols and resets the bias to zero.

This module acts as an 8-bit lookup table that maps input values 0–7 to output values 1–8. It has an 8-bit input port and an 8-bit output port. Inside, an always block sensitive to the input uses a case statement with eight explicit branches. Because no default branch exists, inputs outside 0–7 leave the output unchanged, inferring a latch.

This module wraps a Xilinx FIFO to provide a ready/valid handshake interface for 8-bit streaming data, clocked by clk_in. Ports include 8-bit inputData_in with inputValid_in and inputReady_out, and 8-bit outputData_out with outputValid_out and outputReady_in. Internally, the FIFO's full flag is inverted to form inputReady_out and its empty flag inverted to form outputValid_out, while valid/ready signals drive the FIFO's write and read enables. Transfers occur when both valid and ready are high on a clock edge.

This module implements a purely combinational unsigned 23-bit multiplier. It has two 23-bit unsigned inputs, representing the multiplicand and multiplier, and one 46-bit unsigned output for their product. Internally, the output is directly assigned the arithmetic product of the two inputs, with no registers or sequential logic.

This module is intended as a bidirectional I/O buffer. Its ports are a bidirectional DATA pin, an IOCTR direction control input, an INPUT output for the value read from DATA, and an OUTPUT input for the value to drive onto DATA. Internally it contains two continuous assignments, one for INPUT and one for DATA, but both are incomplete with missing source expressions. Therefore, the module as given has no defined behavior until those assignments are completed to implement the intended direction-controlled bus interface.

This module is a basic function block that reacts to an input change event by copying the sampled input value to its output. Its ports are clock, reset, enable, sync, the event input `rx_change_eI`, data input `rx_I`, event output `tx_change_eO`, data output `tx_O`, and `done`. On a sync pulse with `rx_change_eI` asserted, `rx_I` is sampled and stored. When enabled, a single-state controller pulses a one-shot algorithm that copies the stored value to `tx_O` and emits `tx_change_eO`. The `done` signal indicates algorithm completion and idle status.

The delta_delay module is a parameterized combinational delay element that propagates a single-bit signal from input A to output Z through a chain of continuous assignments, modeling delta-cycle behavior. It has one 1-bit input A, one 1-bit output Z, and a 32-bit parameter N (default 1) that controls the chain length. Internally, an array of intermediate wires is driven from A, with a generate loop cascading each wire to the next, and the final wire drives Z. The output therefore follows the input after the configured number of delta stages, with no sequential or clocked logic.

This module implements an 8-way one-bit demultiplexer. It has an 8-bit select input, a single data input, and eight one-bit registered outputs. A case statement routes the data input to one output for select values 0 through 7, while other select values do nothing. The always block is sensitive only to select, so data-input changes alone do not update outputs until select changes. Unselected outputs retain their previous values.
Response:
module dmux(
input wire [7:0] i_select,
input wire i,
output reg o_0,
output reg o_1,
output reg o_2,
output reg o_3,
output reg o_4,
output reg o_5,
output reg o_6,
output reg o_7
);
  always @(i_select) begin
    case(i_select)
    8'h00 : begin
      o_0 <= i;
    end
    8'h01 : begin
      o_1 <= i;
    end
    8'h02 : begin
      o_2 <= i;
    end
    8'h03 : begin
      o_3 <= i;
    end
    8'h04 : begin
      o_4 <= i;
    end
    8'h05 : begin
      o_5 <= i;
    end
    8'h06 : begin
      o_6 <= i;
    end
    8'h07 : begin
      o_7 <= i;
    end
    default : begin
      // do nothing
    end
    endcase
  end
endmodule

Instruction: D_LATCH is a three-channel 4-bit data register controlled by LATCH_EN. It has one enable input, three 4-bit data inputs, and three corresponding 4-bit registered outputs. Its logic triggers only on changes of LATCH_EN: when high, each output loads its matching input; otherwise all outputs clear to zero. Because the data inputs are not in the sensitivity list, input changes while LATCH_EN stays high do not update the outputs. It therefore captures inputs on the rising edge of LATCH_EN and holds or clears them based only on that enable.

EPROC_IN4 is a selectable 4-bit input encoder/processor that converts EDATA_IN into a 10-bit DATA_OUT with a ready flag. Inputs are bitCLK, bitCLKx2/x4 clocks, rst, ENA, a 2-bit ENCODING select, and 4-bit EDATA_IN; outputs are 10-bit DATA_OUT, DATA_RDY, and busyOut. Internally it instantiates a direct pass-through path and a DEC8b10b decoder, then muxes their results according to ENCODING (00 direct, 01 8b10b, 10 HDLC stub, 11 zeros). A RESTART signal combines rst with inverted ENA, and generate parameters enable or disable the logic, forcing outputs low when disabled.

This module is a top-level wrapper for an 8-bit counter, exposing the counter value on an LED output bus. It has clock, clear, and count inputs, plus an 8-bit output. Internally, it instantiates a counter and directly connects those top-level control signals to it. The counter’s output is routed straight to the LED port, with no extra logic.

This module gates a computer’s USB data lines onto a USB output pair under control of a lock signal. Its inputs are usbClk, rst, computerDataPlus, computerDataMinus, computerLock, clk, and eop; its outputs are computerDataPlusOutput and computerDataMinusOutput. Internally it synchronizes the computer data and eop inputs into the clk domain and double-registers usbClk to detect USB activity or idle. Combinational next-state logic forwards the synchronized data when computerLock is asserted and eop is low, forces both outputs low during eop, and otherwise drives the idle state of D+ high and D- low. The output registers update on USB clock activity or eop, and an asynchronous active-low reset initializes them to idle.

This module is a pipeline register that transfers execute-stage results into the memory stage, synchronized to the clock with an asynchronous active-low reset.

Its inputs are clock, reset, enable, the EXE ALU result, destination register, three control flags (AccMEM, memWE, regWE), EXE data, and a MEM_RAM2 control; outputs are the registered MEM versions of those signals.

On each rising edge, if enabled and MEM_RAM2 is low, all EXE inputs are latched to the outputs. Otherwise, when MEM_RAM2 is high, the AccMEM, memWE, and regWE outputs are forced low; reset also clears those three flags.

This module implements a single-bit logical inverter. It has one input, `a`, and one output, `y`. Internally, it continuously drives the output with the logical complement of the input. The output updates combinationally whenever the input changes.

This module is a synthesis wrapper for a 40K block-memory example design. It has inputs CLK_IN and RESET_IN, plus a 9-bit STATUS output. Internally it synchronizes reset, generates memory stimulus, and checks read data using stimulus-generator and checker blocks. STATUS[7:0] accumulates checker issue flags, while STATUS[8] reflects a delayed stimulus-flow signal. Write-enable, data, and address are registered before driving the block-memory instance.

This module is a 4-to-16 demultiplexer that routes a 16-bit input word to exactly one of sixteen 16-bit outputs selected by a 4-bit selector. It has a 4-bit Selector input, a 16-bit input bus, and sixteen 16-bit outputs labeled output_A through output_P. Combinational logic drives the selected output with the input value and forces all unselected outputs to zero. Selector values 0000 through 1111 map to output_A through output_P, respectively.
Response:
module Demultiplexer_4x16(
input wire [3:0] Selector,
input wire [15:0] input,
output reg [15:0] output_A,
output reg [15:0] output_B,
output reg [15:0] output_C,
output reg [15:0] output_D,
output reg [15:0] output_E,
output reg [15:0] output_F,
output reg [15:0] output_G,
output reg [15:0] output_H,

Instruction: This module implements a simple two-input OR gate. Its inputs are single-bit signals `a` and `b`, and its output is a single-bit signal `y`. The output is driven combinationally to high whenever either input is high. It contains no sequential or state-holding logic.

The module is named scrambler but contains no scrambling logic. Its ports are clk, en, reset, seed, and d_in as inputs plus d_out as output, though only clk is actually used; d_out is never driven. Internally, a parameterized register array (ARRAY_WIDTH rows of BUS_WIDTH bits) acts as a shift register, shifting on each rising clock edge and inserting a constant all-zero vector into the lowest position. The en, reset, seed, and d_in signals are ignored.

This module implements a 4-bit magnitude comparator. It takes two 4-bit unsigned inputs, n1 and n2, and produces three single-bit outputs: g, e, and l. The internal combinational logic drives g high when n1 is greater than n2, e high when the inputs are equal, and l high when n1 is less than n2, with only one output asserted at a time.

This module implements a technology-selectable clock gate. Its inputs are the clock i and enable en, and its output o is the gated clock; parameters tech and ren configure the implementation. When ren=1, en is registered on the falling edge of i; when ren=0, it is used combinationally. Depending on tech, it instantiates vendor-specific clock-gating cells (Xilinx or UMC) or falls back to ANDing i with the enable.

module clkand(
input wire i,
input wire en,
output wire o
);
parameter [31:0] tech=0;
parameter [31:0] ren=0;
// registered enable
reg eni;
  generate if (ren == 1) begin: re
      always @(negedge i) begin
      eni <= en;
    end
  end
  endgenerate
  generate if (ren == 0) begin: ce
      assign eni = en;
  end
  endgenerate
  generate if ((tech == virtex2) || (tech == spartan3) || (tech == spartan3e) || (tech == virtex4) || (tech == virtex5)) begin: xil
      clkand_unisim clkgate(
          .I(i),
      .en(eni),
      .O(o));
  end
  endgenerate
  generate if ((tech == ut25)) begin: ut
      clkand_ut025crh clkgate(
          .I(i),
      .en(eni),
      .O(o));
  end
  endgenerate
  generate if (has_clkand[tech] == 0) begin: gen
      assign o = i & eni;
  end
  endgenerate
endmodule

Instruction: This module is a 3-bit equality comparator. It has one output, `eq`, and two 3-bit inputs, `in0` and `in1`. Internally, it compares the two inputs and drives `eq` high when they are equal, and low when they differ. The comparison result is computed through an intermediate wire before being passed to the output.

This module is a VGA timing generator for a 640×480 display. It accepts a clock and reset input and outputs horizontal sync, vertical sync, an active-video indicator, a pixel tick enable, and 10-bit pixel X/Y coordinates. Internally, a divide-by-two stage generates the pixel tick, while horizontal and vertical counters track timing through the front porch, sync pulse, back porch, and visible display regions. The sync outputs are registered to avoid glitches, and the video-on signal is asserted only during the visible 640×480 area. Reset clears the internal counters and sync outputs.

Converts a 4-bit binary/hex digit into a 7-bit pattern for a common-anode seven-segment display. Input `binary_value` is 4 bits; output `sevenSeg` is a 7-bit registered signal, one bit per segment. A combinational block sensitive to input changes uses a case statement to map each of the 16 input values to its segment pattern, with a default all-off pattern. The mapping covers 0–9 and A–F, though some codes (such as 8 and 1011) produce identical patterns.

This module implements a positive-edge-triggered D flip-flop with a synchronous active-high reset. Its inputs are data `d`, clock `clk`, and reset `r`; outputs are `q` and its complement `q_n`. On each rising clock edge, the stored state is cleared to 0 when reset is high, otherwise it loads `d`. The registered state drives `q`, while `q_n` is its logical inverse.

This module is a 16-bit ALU that performs addition, subtraction, set-less-than and negation according to a 4-bit operation code. Its inputs are two 16-bit operands and the 4-bit operation selector; its outputs are the 16-bit result plus carry, zero, negative and less-than flags. Internally, a 4-to-1 multiplexer selects among the sum, difference, set-less-than and negate results produced by a sub-module. Sign-extended 17-bit operands generate the addition carry, while the zero, negative and less-than flags are derived from the result and compare signals.

This module is a 40-word by 32-bit register file with two read ports and one write port. Its inputs are two 6-bit read addresses, a 6-bit write address, 32-bit write data, and a reset; its outputs are the two 32-bit read-data values. The storage array’s word zero is forced to zero. On reset, the array and both read outputs are cleared. Otherwise, a nonzero write address stores the write data, and the outputs present the words selected by the two read addresses; writes to word zero are ignored.

The module implements a three-state clocked handshake controller with asynchronous reset. Its inputs are RESET, CLK, REQ, DRDY, and ARDY; outputs are ACK and EN. From an idle state waiting for REQ, the FSM advances when REQ and ARDY are asserted, then either waits for DRDY or completes directly if DRDY is already high. After DRDY, it waits for REQ to clear while asserting ACK. EN is asserted only in the idle state when REQ is high.

This module implements a digital pulse-width modulator that produces a variable-duty-cycle square wave from an 8-bit duty value. It has a clock input, an 8-bit input setting the duty cycle, and a single registered PWM output. A free-running counter increments on every clock edge, and its upper bits form a periodically ramping reference. The output is driven high while this reference value is less than the input, and low otherwise, so the input directly controls the output's duty cycle.

This module is a combinational 4-bit inverter. It has one 4-bit input bus, `A`, and one 4-bit output bus, `F`. Each bit of the output is the logical complement of the corresponding bit of the input. There is no clocking or sequential state; the output follows the input continuously.

Converts a PS/2 keyboard scancode into a 32-bit clock divisor corresponding to a musical note frequency. It has an 8-bit scancode input and a registered 32-bit clock_divisor output. A level-sensitive case statement maps specific scancodes to fixed divisors for notes d', e', f', g', a', and h'. Any unmatched scancode defaults to the divisor for c' at 264 Hz. The output updates whenever the scancode changes.

This module implements a 4-bit wide 2-to-1 multiplexer. It has two 4-bit data inputs, x1 and x2, a 1-bit select input, sel, and a 4-bit output, y. Its combinational always block is sensitive to both data inputs and the select. When sel is low, y is assigned x1; otherwise, y is assigned x2.
Response:
module mux_2_to_1_4bit(
input wire [3:0] x1,
input wire [3:0] x2,
input wire sel,
output reg [3:0] y
);
  always @(x1, x2, sel) begin
    case(sel)
    1'b0 : begin
      y <= x1;
    end
    default : begin
      y <= x2;
    end
    endcase
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module implements a UART receiver that converts a serial RX line into an 8-bit parallel output. It has CLK and asynchronous RESET inputs, a serial RX input, an S_TICK oversampling enable, a RX_DONE_TICK output, and an 8-bit DOUT output. Internally, a four-state finite state machine (idle, start, data, stop) samples RX at S_TICK intervals. It detects a start bit, shifts in DBIT data bits LSB-first, then waits SB_TICK stop-bit ticks and asserts RX_DONE_TICK. The data register is exposed on DOUT.

This module computes a combined carry-generate signal for carry-lookahead logic: it indicates whether a carry is produced locally or propagated from a prior stage. It has three 1-bit inputs—local generate `g`, propagate `p`, and previous-stage generate `g_prec`—and one 1-bit output `g_out`. The output is asserted when either the local generate is true, or propagation is true and the previous generate is true. The logic is purely combinational.

This module implements a two-input logical OR gate. It has two 1-bit inputs, in1 and in2, and one 1-bit output, outOr. The output is driven combinationally to the logical OR of the two inputs, so outOr is high whenever either input is high. There is no clocking or stored state; changes on either input immediately affect the output.

This module implements the DES PC-1 key permutation. It takes a 64-bit key input, indexed as `[1:64]`, and produces two 28-bit outputs, `c0x` and `d0x`. Internally, it reorders 56 selected key bits into a 56-bit vector according to the PC-1 bit order, effectively discarding parity bits. The vector is then split into two halves: `c0x` receives bits 1–28 and `d0x` receives bits 29–56. The design is purely combinational.

This module is intended to act as a single-bit inverter, driving the output with the logical complement of the input. It has one 1-bit input and one 1-bit output. Internally, an always block performs the inversion using a nonblocking assignment. However, the sensitivity and assignment identifiers are case-mismatched from the declared ports, so the actual output is not driven by this logic.

The module implements a 13-bit up counter for Ascon round, function, and sub-iteration sequencing. It has a clock input, an active-low asynchronous reset, and a count-enable input. Its outputs expose the counter as a 4-bit round number, a 3-bit function selector, and a 6-bit sub-iteration index. On each rising clock edge, the internal counter increments only when enabled; otherwise it holds. A low reset asynchronously clears the counter to zero.

This module is a countdown timer whose maximum time depends on a 2-bit difficulty input. Its inputs are a 50 MHz clock, the difficulty setting, and an asynchronous reset; outputs are 8-bit remaining and current count values. A clock converter produces a 1 Hz tick, and difficulty selects maximum values of 30, 20, 10, or 5. Each tick increments the counter, reset clears it, and the counter wraps to zero after reaching the maximum. The remaining output is the maximum minus the current count.

This module is a simple pass-through bridge for JTAG signals. It forwards the cy_tck, cy_tms, and cy_tdi inputs directly to the sys_tck, sys_tms, and sys_tdi outputs, while routing the sys_tdo input back to the cy_tdo output. All connections are purely combinational, with no storage, clocking, or additional control logic. The design effectively connects a cy-side JTAG controller to a sys-side JTAG target.

This module generates a periodic refresh strobe by dividing the input clock. Its ports are a high-active asynchronous reset, Rst; the input clock, Clk; and the registered output, ClkOut. Internally, a 32-bit counter increments on each Clk rising edge until it reaches CtaMax, derived from Fosc/Fdiv. When the terminal count is reached, the counter clears and ClkOut pulses high for one clock cycle; otherwise ClkOut stays low. Thus ClkOut is a one-cycle-wide refresh pulse, not a 50%-duty clock.

This module is a combinational hexadecimal-to-7-segment display decoder. It accepts a 4-bit input A representing a hex digit (0–F) and produces a 7-bit output Y containing the corresponding active-high segment pattern. Internally, a nested conditional (priority mux) maps each of the 16 input values to a fixed segment code, with a default pattern for any unlisted input.

Magnitude_Comparator is a 4-bit combinational comparator that compares inputs A and B and produces three comparison flags. Its ports are 4-bit inputs A and B and outputs AgtB, AeqB, and AltB. Inside, an always block triggered by A or B uses a local 3-bit Tmp, initialized to zero, then sets Tmp[2] when A>B, Tmp[1] when A==B, otherwise Tmp[0]. The outputs are assigned from Tmp as AgtB=Tmp[0], AeqB=Tmp[1], and AltB=Tmp[2], so the bit-to-output mapping is crossed relative to the comparison comments.

This module implements a small synchronous finite state machine whose 4-bit state register is updated by a D flip-flop block on the KEY[1] clock, with KEY[0] used as reset. Its inputs are KEY[3:0], and its outputs are the 7-segment display HEX0 and the 10-bit LEDR bus. Combinational next-state logic drives the register; the state bit QQ[3] is tied low, making it effectively a 3-bit state machine. The current state is routed to LEDR's lower four bits and decoded by a 7-segment decoder to drive HEX0.

This module is a simple combinational passthrough that copies a 5-bit input value directly to a 5-bit output. Its ports are `dips_i`, a 5-bit input, and `leds_o`, a 5-bit output. Internally, each input bit is continuously assigned to the corresponding output bit, so the output always matches the input with no inversion, storage, or other logic.

This module is a self-test wrapper for a RAM block: it generates write/read stimulus, captures the RAM read data, and reports checker issues. Its ports are a clock input, a reset input, and a 9-bit status output. Internally, it synchronizes reset, instantiates a stimulus generator, a data checker, and the RAM port. It pipelines write enable, address, and data into the RAM while counting write activity. STATUS[7:0] latches checker flags, and STATUS[8] is a delayed stimulus-flow status bit.

This module implements a two-input exclusive-OR (XOR) gate. It has two 1-bit inputs, A and B, and one 1-bit output, Z. The output Z is driven combinationally to be high whenever A and B differ, and low whenever they are equal. No state or sequential elements are present.

This is a combinational 16-bit logical unit. It takes two 16-bit operands, RA and RB, plus a 3-bit opcode OP, and produces a 16-bit result LOG_OUT and a 4-bit status output SREG_OUT. Depending on OP, it selects bitwise OR (011), AND (010), AND (110), or a move of RB (100), defaulting to OR. The intended zero flag is derived from the result, but its expression always evaluates to 1, so the only driven status bit, SREG_OUT[2], is stuck high while the other status bits are undriven.

This module implements a tri-state buffer. It has a data input A, an enable input E, and an output Z. When E is high, Z follows A; when E is low, Z is driven to high impedance. For any other E value, Z is also high impedance.

The module is intended to implement a 2-input NOR gate. It has inputs `a` and `b`, and output `z`. Internally, it computes the negation of their logical OR, but assigns that result to an undeclared uppercase `Z` instead of the declared output `z`, leaving `z` effectively undriven.

This module is a top-level FIFO wrapper that selects either synchronous or asynchronous FIFO behavior based on the `async_i` input. It has write-side ports `wclk_i`, `wrst_i`, `wen_i`, and 8-bit `data_i`, plus flags `full_o`, `afull_o`, and `overflow_o`. The read side has `rclk_i`, `rrst_i`, `ren_i`, 8-bit `data_o`, and flags `empty_o`, `aempty_o`, `underflow_o`, and `valid_o`. Internally, it instantiates two depth-4 FIFO cores, one synchronous and one asynchronous, and multiplexes their status and data outputs according to `async_i`. The synchronous instance uses the write clock and reset for both write and read domains.

This module implements a simple single-bit buffer. It has one input port, a, and one output port, b. Internally, the output is directly assigned from the input, so b always follows a. There is no clock, reset, or stored state. Its behavior is purely combinational and performs no logical transformation.

Implements a priority interrupt controller for an 80xx-style CPU. Inputs are clk, reset, four IRQ lines, interrupt-acknowledge and fetch strobes, and write-enable/address/data for programming; outputs are the interrupt-request line and an 8-bit data bus. Internally it edge-detects enabled IRQ inputs, latches them as pending until acknowledged, and applies fixed priority with IRQ0 highest. A CPU-writable enable register gates each IRQ; on acknowledge the highest-priority pending source is cleared and a hardcoded RST vector is returned, otherwise the enable register is read back.

The cpu module is a pipelined processor subsystem that interfaces to an external system bus. Its inputs are CLK, interrupt requests IRQ/NMI, read data Din, and ready RDY; outputs are interrupt acknowledges IAK/NAK, memory enable MEME, read/write RW, address ADDR, write data Dout, and transaction type DTYPE. Internally, a clock divider generates multiple clocks and cache-enable, a pipeline executes instructions and issues separate instruction/data accesses, a TLB translates addresses and marks cacheability, and a cache arbitrates those accesses onto the external bus while handling stalls.

This module implements a combinational multiplier. It takes a 32-bit input `in_a` and a 16-bit input `in_b`, and produces a 32-bit output `result`. Internally, the full product is computed into a 48-bit temporary value. The output is then driven by the lower 32 bits of that product, discarding the upper bits.

This module implements a digital clock. It takes a clock and reset as inputs and produces an 8-bit seven-segment display drive plus a 4-bit digit-select multiplexer output. Internally, a divider generates a 1 Hz clock, a time counter tracks hour and minute digits, and a seven-segment controller converts those digits into display and multiplexing signals. The counter outputs are zero-extended to match the display controller’s input widths.

This module implements a combinational 32-bit adder. It has two 32-bit input operands, Op1 and Op2, and a 32-bit output, R. Whenever either input changes, the module assigns the arithmetic sum of the two operands to R. No clock, reset, or sequential state is used; R continuously reflects the addition result.

This module acts as a simple single-bit pass-through buffer. It has one input, `sw1`, and one output, `led8`. Internally, the output is directly connected to the input, so the LED reflects the switch state continuously. There is no clocked logic, storage, or additional processing.

A 64-bit barrel shifter pipelined across three stages, controlled by a 6-bit shift amount. Inputs are sysclk, async active-high reset, enable, 64-bit inbus and 6-bit shift; output is 64-bit outbus. The first two combinational stages shift by 0–3 and 0/4/8/12. A clock-enabled register holds the intermediate result and the top two shift bits. The final combinational stage shifts by 0/16/32/48 using the registered bits; reset clears the pipeline.

This module is a combinational seven-segment display decoder driven by a one-hot input. It has a 7-bit input `entrada` and a 7-bit output `display`. Internally, it compares the input against seven one-hot patterns representing values 0 through 6, selecting the corresponding active-low segment code for each. Any unrecognized input defaults to the segment pattern for 7. The selected code is continuously assigned to the output.

The papilio1_top module is a Papilio-1 FPGA top-level SoC integrating an 8086-class CPU core, 40 KB block RAM, a bootstrap ROM, and a 16550-style UART. Its ports are a clock input, serial rx/tx, and three 16-bit bidirectional wing headers (W1A, W1B, W2C). A DCM multiplies the input clock to 40 MHz to drive the CPU, while address decoding selects the UART (0x3F8) or bootstrap ROM and multiplexes their read data onto the CPU bus. UART interrupts are latched from the rx line, and status/debug signals plus LEDs are routed to header pins.

This module implements a single-bit half adder. It has two 1-bit inputs, a and b, and two 1-bit outputs, sum and carry. The sum output is the exclusive-OR of the inputs, while the carry output is their logical AND. The design is purely combinational, using continuous assignments to produce both outputs.

This FSM sequences a counter-driven search/access operation. Inputs are the flags g, e, and l, clk, reset, counter_done, and free; outputs are sel_1, sel_2, counter_reset, counter_enable, load, done, and rwbar. A registered state (RESET0, RESET1, WAITING, S1–S5) advances on the clock, with next-state and output logic in a second block. Reset clears the counter and sets defaults; S1–S3 load and run the counter, S4 sets sel_2 and rwbar from g/e/l, and S5 asserts done, looping through WAITING until free restarts the cycle.

This module is a button-triggered delayed pulse detector. It has a button input, a clock input, and a registered output S. Internally, a 24-bit counter increments on each rising clock edge while the button is high or while an in-progress count continues after release. When the counter reaches 10,000,000, S is asserted for one clock cycle and the counter is cleared; otherwise S stays low.

This module bridges a 12-bit ADC/microphone data stream to an SPI slave interface. Inputs are clock, spi_clk, spi_cs, adc_data, and fmexg_mic_sync; outputs are spi_miso, adc_clk, adc_pdwn, and interrupt. Internally it divides the clock by 12 to generate adc_clk, writes ADC data (or a fixed marker when mic sync is high) into a FIFO, and reads the FIFO using SPI timing. SPI bit/byte counters shift two 12-bit samples into 24-bit serial data on spi_miso, while interrupt asserts when the FIFO is almost full.

This module is a partial VGA timing generator. It accepts a 100 MHz input clock and outputs a 3-bit LED bus, three 4-bit VGA color buses, and horizontal/vertical sync signals. Internally, a clock divider is intended to create a 25.175 MHz pixel clock, while horizontal and vertical counters track pixel counts and reset at configured line/frame lengths. The LEDs act as debug flags for the pixel clock, end-of-line, and end-of-frame events. The VGA color and sync outputs are declared but left undriven.

This module is a clocked hexadecimal-to-BCD converter. It takes a 16-bit value formed from four 4-bit switch inputs (`sw0`–`sw3`) and a clock (`CLK`), producing four registered BCD digit outputs (`bcd0`–`bcd3`). On each rising clock edge, it applies the double-dabble algorithm: any BCD nibble at least 5 has 3 added, then all nibbles and the binary value are shifted left over 16 iterations. Only the lowest four BCD digits (ones through thousands) are output; higher digits are computed internally but discarded.

LAB7a is a 4-bit finite state machine. Its inputs are KEY[3:0]; outputs are HEX0[6:0] and LEDR[9:0]. Combinational logic computes the next state from the current state, and a 4-bit D flip-flop register (controlled by KEY[1:0]) stores it. The registered state drives LEDR’s lower four bits, with the upper six bits zero, and is decoded by a seven-segment decoder to HEX0. KEY[3:2] are unused.

This module is a combinational hexadecimal-to-7-segment decoder. It takes a 4-bit input A and produces a 7-bit output Q for active-low segment drives. A case statement maps each input value 0–F to the corresponding 7-segment pattern. Any undefined input defaults to the pattern for digit 0.

This module implements a combinational 2-to-1 multiplexer intended to select one of two inputs based on a select line. It has a 2-bit input bus, a single select input, and a registered output. The always block is sensitive to both the select and input bus, and a case statement drives the output from bit 0 when the select is low and from bit 1 when it is high. As written, the case expression does not use the declared select port, so the selection may not work as intended unless that mismatch is corrected.

module MUX2x1vi(
input wire [1:0] I,
input wire S,
output reg O
);
  always @(S, I) begin
    case(s)
    1'b0 : begin
      O <= I[0];
    end
    1'b1 : begin
      O <= I[1];
    end
    default : begin
    end
    endcase
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module is a voice-scanning controller that sequentially selects SID voices. Inputs are clock, active-high reset, and start_iter; outputs are the 4-bit voice_osc index and enable_osc. A parameter sets the number of voices, default eight. On reset, the voice counter clears and enable_osc is low. A start_iter pulse clears the counter and raises enable_osc; thereafter the counter increments each clock until it reaches the last voice, then wraps to zero and drops enable_osc.

This module generates and conditions the clocks for an Ethernet MAC example design. It accepts a differential input clock (clk_in_p/n) and an asynchronous global reset (glbl_rst), and produces three clocks—gtx_clk_bufg, s_axi_aclk, and refclk_bufg—plus a dcm_locked status output. The input pair is buffered and routed through a BUFGCE, then fed to a clocking wizard that synthesizes all output clocks. A synchronizer and falling-edge detector resynchronize the MMCM LOCKED signal into the input clock domain and merge it with the global reset, which is debounced by a reset synchronizer before driving the MMCM reset. The MMCM lock indication is also passed directly to dcm_locked.

This module implements a two-input AND gate used as a glitch-prevention primitive in the openMSP430 design. It has two 1-bit inputs, a and b, and one 1-bit output, y. The output is simply the logical AND of the two inputs. The module is instantiated at glitch-sensitive points to stop synthesis from merging surrounding combinatorial logic into glitchy clouds.

Computes the addresses of the four orthogonally neighboring cells around a given position on an 8×8 grid. Inputs `my_x` and `my_y` are 3-bit coordinates; outputs `addr_up`, `addr_dw`, `addr_rg`, and `addr_lf` are 6-bit addresses. Internally, 3-bit increment and decrement blocks generate x/y±1 with wraparound, and each neighbor address is formed by concatenating the appropriate y coordinate with the x coordinate.

This module is a pulse-stretcher: when input transitions to HOLD_LEVEL, output holds that level for HOLD_TIME clock cycles, then follows input. Ports: clk, active-low async resetn, active-high sync clear sraz, input, output, and holding. A counter is cleared by resetn or sraz, else loads HOLD_TIME-1 on a qualifying transition and decrements each clock while nonzero. Output selects input when the counter is zero, otherwise the captured input value; holding flags counter activity. HOLD_TIME and HOLD_LEVEL are parameters.

This module is a frequency divider/sampling generator. Its inputs are clock, zera (clear/reset), and conta (count enable). Its outputs are amostra (sample pulse), conta4 (2-bit modulo-4 count), and conta8 (3-bit modulo-8 count). Internally, a modulo-4 counter and a modulo-8 counter share the same clock, reset, and enable; their terminal outputs are XORed to produce amostra.
